derivations.claim: The orbit map $G\to N$, $g\mapsto\operatorname{Ad}(g)e$, has irreducible image closure. By [F1] its image has dimension $\dim\mathfrak g-\dim Z_{\mathfrak g}(e)=2|\Phi^+|=\dim N$; by [F6] the constructible image is dense and therefore contains a nonempty open subset of the irreducible variety $N$. The orbit is $G$-stable, so its translates of this open subset cover the orbit; consequently $G\cdot e$ is open in $N$.

The Springer map is $$\mu:G\times^B\mathfrak n^+\longrightarrow N,\qquad[g,x]\longmapsto\operatorname{Ad}(g)x.$$ Its graph is the incidence subvariety $$\{(gB,y)\in X\times N:y\in\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak n^+\},$$ which is closed because the spaces $\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak n^+$ form a vector subbundle of $X\times\mathfrak g$. The projection $X\times N\to N$ is projective by [F4], so $\mu$ is proper by the projective-morphism theorem included in [F4]. Surjectivity follows from the last clause of [F1].

If $y\in N\setminus G\cdot e$, conjugate it into $\mathfrak n^+$ by [F1]. At least one simple-root coefficient must vanish by [F2]. For each simple $\alpha_i$, set $\mathfrak n_i= igoplus_{ eta\in\Phi^+,\, eta
e\alpha_i}\mathfrak g_ eta$. This is a nilpotent Lie subalgebra. It is an ideal in $\mathfrak p_{\alpha_i}=\mathfrak b\oplus\mathfrak g_{-\alpha_i}$: brackets with $\mathfrak h$ preserve each root space; brackets with positive root spaces have weights $ eta+\gamma$, which if nonzero remain positive and cannot equal $\alpha_i$ because $ eta
e\alpha_i$ has a positive coefficient at another simple root; and if $ eta-\alpha_i$ is a root for $ eta
e\alpha_i$, it must be positive, since otherwise $\alpha_i$ would be a sum of positive roots. These assertions use [F5] and the simple-root basis. The exponential/BCH coordinates in [F5] identify $\exp:\mathfrak n^+	o U$ as a polynomial isomorphism, so $N_i=\exp(\mathfrak n_i)$ is a closed connected unipotent subgroup with Lie algebra $\mathfrak n_i$. Order the positive-root coordinates with $\alpha_i$ first. The product of the remaining root subgroups is then a closed subvariety of $U$ of dimension $|\Phi^+|-1$; it lies in $N_i$, which has the same dimension, so equals $N_i$. Hence $U=U_{\alpha_i}N_i$. Since $\mathfrak n_i$ is an ideal, its normalizer in the connected group $P_{\alpha_i}$ has full Lie algebra and hence equals $P_{\alpha_i}$; thus $N_i$ is normal in $P_{\alpha_i}$. The quotient $P_{\alpha_i}/N_i$ is generated by $T$ and the images of $U_{\alpha_i}$ and $U_{-\alpha_i}$. The rank-one homomorphism of [[lem-semisimple-rank-one-sl2-root-homomorphism]] supplies the semisimple rank-one subgroup. The central subtorus $(\ker\alpha_i)^0\subseteq T$ centralizes it, and $\alpha_i\circ\alpha_i^\vee(t)=t^2$ shows that its quotient in $T$ is covered by the coroot torus up to finite index. Hence $P_{\alpha_i}/N_i$ is a central product of a torus and a semisimple rank-one group, so it is reductive and has no nontrivial connected normal unipotent subgroup. By [[def-radical-and-unipotent-radical-of-an-algebraic-group]], $N_i$ is the unipotent radical of $P_{\alpha_i}$. It is therefore $P_{\alpha_i}$-stable and has dimension $|\Phi^+|-1$. Thus $N\setminus G\cdot e$ is contained in the finite union of the images of $$G	imes^{P_{\alpha_i}}N_i\longrightarrow N,\qquad[g,u]\longmapsto\operatorname{Ad}(g)\log u.$$ Here $\log:N_i	o\mathfrak n_i$ is the polynomial inverse of the exponential just constructed; it is $P_{\alpha_i}$-equivariant by conjugation, so the displayed map is well-defined. Each source has dimension $(|\Phi^+|-1)+(|\Phi^+|-1)=2|\Phi^+|-2$ by [F4]. Hence the complement of the open regular orbit has codimension at least two. The Jacobian rank at $e$ is full by the proof of [F1]; $G$-equivariance makes every point of $G\cdot e$ regular. Thus $N$ is regular in codimension one. Since it is an integral complete intersection, [F7] gives normality.

The fiber over $e$ is a single point. Indeed, if $e\in\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak n^+$, write $g=b_1n_wb_2$ by [F3]. The element $x=\operatorname{Ad}(b_1^{-1})e$ still has every simple coefficient nonzero by [F2]. Since $\operatorname{Ad}(n_w^{-1})x\in\mathfrak n^+$, each nonzero simple-root component of $x$ must map to a positive root space; distinct root spaces cannot cancel. Therefore $w^{-1}$ sends every positive simple root to a positive root, so $w=1$ by [F3], and $gB=B$. This algebraic argument holds after every algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb C$ as well. Equivariance gives a singleton geometric fiber over every point of $O=G\cdot e$. The restriction $\mu_O:\mu^{-1}(O)\to O$ is proper by base change. Its fibers are finite type and their geometric point sets are singletons, so each fiber point is isolated and has residue field finite over the base residue field; the finite-fiber criterion in [F8] makes $\mu_O$ quasi-finite, and proper quasi-finite finiteness in [F8] makes it finite. Both source and target are integral of dimension $2|\Phi^+|$, so the induced function-field extension is finite. It is separable in characteristic zero, and by [F9] has a primitive element $\theta$. After replacing an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq O$ by a smaller nonempty principal open, its finite preimage is $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite over $A$, $\theta$ lies in $B$, and $B=A[\theta]\cong A[T]/(f)$ for the monic minimal polynomial $f$ of $\theta$: first clear denominators to place $\theta$ in $B$, then localize to kill the finite torsion quotient $B/A[\theta]$ and to put the coefficients of $f$ in $A$. The discriminant of $f$ is nonzero by separability, so after inverting it this finite map is étale of rank $d=[\operatorname{Frac}B:\operatorname{Frac}A]$. Every geometric closed fiber in this open then has $d$ distinct points, but every geometric fiber over $O$ is a singleton; therefore $d=1$. This proves birationality without inferring degree from a closed-point count alone.

Let $R=\mathbb C[N]$ and $S=\Gamma(T^*X,\mathcal O)$. Properness makes $S=\Gamma(N,\mu_*\mathcal O_{T^*X})$ a finite $R$-algebra by [F10]. Birationality embeds $S$ in $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and contains $R$. Every element of a finite $R$-algebra is integral over $R$ by the determinant trick. Since $R$ is integrally closed by step 2.1, $S=R$. This proves the Springer-functions isomorphism without inferring regularity of a rational function from connected fibers.

citations.quote:
Fix a positive root system $\Phi^+$ as in [[thm-triangular-decomposition-from-a-chosen-positive-root-system]]. The **Weyl vector** for that choice is

$$\rho:=\frac12\sum_{\alpha\in \Phi^+} \alpha \in \mathfrak h^*.$$

This is the shift used in the dot action and in the quadratic Casimir eigenvalue formula on this page.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be the connected simply connected complex
semisimple affine algebraic group with maximal torus $T$, root system $\Phi$,
positive system $\Phi^+$, Borel subgroup $B=T\ltimes U$, opposite unipotent
subgroup $U^-$ and Weyl group $W=N_G(T)/T$ of
[[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]] and
[[lem-semisimple-borel-root-factorization]], fix a simple root
$\alpha\in\Delta$ with minimal parabolic $P_\alpha$ as in
[[lem-semisimple-minimal-parabolic-root-subgroup]], put
$U^-_\alpha=\prod_{\beta\in\Phi^+,\ \beta\neq\alpha}U_{-\beta}$, and let
$X_B=G/B\subseteq\mathbb P(W_B)$ and
$X_\alpha=G/P_\alpha\subseteq\mathbb P(W_\alpha)$ be the closed orbits with
orbit maps $\pi_B:G\to X_B$, $\pi_\alpha:G\to X_\alpha$ of
[[lem-semisimple-projective-orbit-flag-quotients]]. Write
$\Omega=U^-B$ for the open big cell. Then:

(i) the orbit map restricted to $\Omega$ factors through the projection
$\Omega\to\Omega/B\cong U^-$ as an injective morphism
$\sigma_B:U^-\to X_B$ with
$\pi_B^{-1}\bigl(\sigma_B(U^-)\bigr)=\Omega$ and
$\sigma_B(U^-)\times B\cong\Omega$ exhibiting $\pi_B$ as the trivial
$B$-torsor over the chart $\sigma_B(U^-)$; the same holds for $\pi_\alpha$ with
the morphism $\sigma_\alpha:U^-_\alpha\to X_\alpha$, $\sigma_\alpha(u)=u[v_\alpha]$,
the subgroup $P_\alpha$ in place of $B$, and the open subset
$U^-_\alpha P_\alpha\subseteq G$ in place of $\Omega$;

(ii) each chart in (i) is a Zariski-open subscheme of its orbit, and all its single $G$-translates cover that orbit. Every translate has the transported product trivialization. Since the projective orbits are quasi-compact, finite subfamilies of these open translates also cover them;

(iii) consequently $\pi_B$ and $\pi_\alpha$ represent Zariski-locally trivial right $B$- and $P_\alpha$-torsors. Their fppf sheaf quotients are $X_B$ and $X_\alpha$, and each associated bundle, including $G\times^B\mathbb C_{-\lambda}$, is Zariski locally trivial on the translated charts.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be the connected simply connected complex
semisimple affine algebraic group with Borel $B=T\ltimes U$ and Weyl group $W$
of [[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]] and
[[lem-semisimple-borel-root-factorization]], and let $\alpha$ be a simple
root with minimal parabolic $P_\alpha=B\sqcup Bn_\alpha B$, root subgroup
$U_{-\alpha}$ and Weyl subgroup $\{1,s_\alpha\}$ as in
[[lem-semisimple-minimal-parabolic-root-subgroup]]. Let
$\pi_B:G\to X_B$ and $\pi_\alpha:G\to X_\alpha$ be the orbit maps of
[[lem-semisimple-projective-orbit-flag-quotients]]. Then:

(i) the induced map $f:X_B\to X_\alpha$, $g[v_B]\mapsto g[v_\alpha]$, is a
surjective morphism of varieties, well defined because $B\subseteq P_\alpha$,
and its fibre over $g[v_\alpha]$ is canonically the coset space
$P_\alpha/B$, which is $\mathbb P^1$ in the two-chart description
$z\mapsto u_{-\alpha}(z)B$, $t\mapsto u_\alpha(t)n_\alpha B$ with $t=z^{-1}$
of [[lem-semisimple-minimal-parabolic-root-subgroup]];

(ii) $f$ is a Zariski-locally trivial fibre bundle with fibre $\mathbb P^1$: over each single $G$-translate $gV$ of the open torsor chart $V=\sigma_\alpha(U^-_\alpha)\subseteq X_\alpha$ from [[lem-semisimple-flag-torsor-zariski-charts]], it becomes the projection $gV\times\mathbb P^1\to gV$. These translates cover $X_\alpha$ and admit a finite subcover. In the rank-one case $G=P_\alpha$, the base is a point and $f$ is the unique map from $\mathbb P^1$ to that point.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the published group and sheaf
suppliers. Let $G$ be a connected simply connected complex semisimple affine
algebraic group, $B\supseteq T$ a Borel subgroup and maximal torus,
$X=G/B$, $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}G$,
$\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}T$, and $\Phi^+$ the positive roots selected by
$B$. Write $\rho=\frac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$. All schemes are over
$\mathbb C$. For an integral weight $\eta$, $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ denotes the
$G$-equivariant line bundle $G\times^B\mathbb C_\eta$ with fiber character
$\eta$ at $eB$.

The infinitesimal $G$-action gives an anchor
$$a_X:\mathcal L_X:=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathfrak g\longrightarrow T_X,\qquad f\otimes x\longmapsto f x_X.$$
Give $\mathcal L_X$ the action-algebroid bracket
$$[f\otimes x,g\otimes y]=fg\otimes[x,y]+f x_X(g)\otimes y-g y_X(f)\otimes x.$$
Its kernel $\mathfrak b_X=\ker a_X$ is the isotropy Lie-algebra bundle; at
$gB$ its fiber is $\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak b$.

For any $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$, the character $\kappa+\rho$ of
$\mathfrak b$ (zero on $\mathfrak n^+$) transports to an
$\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\chi^X_{\kappa+\rho}:\mathfrak b_X\to\mathcal O_X$.
The transport is independent of the representative $g$ of $gB$, since a
character is invariant under the adjoint action of $B$. The action-algebroid
enveloping sheaf $\mathcal U_X(\mathfrak g)$ is generated by $\mathcal O_X$
and $\mathcal L_X$ with the displayed bracket and
$$[x,f]=x_X(f),\qquad x\in\mathcal L_X,\ f\in\mathcal O_X.$$
Define the sheaf of twisted differential operators
$$\mathcal D_\kappa:=\mathcal U_X(\mathfrak g)/\bigl(\xi-\chi^X_{\kappa+\rho}(\xi):\xi\in\mathfrak b_X\bigr).$$
Its order filtration assigns order zero to $\mathcal O_X$ and order at most
one to the image of $\mathcal L_X$. A TDO means a filtered
$\mathcal O_X$-ring with $F_0=\mathcal O_X$, associated graded
$\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X$, and first-order commutator equal to
the anchor; the well-definedness and PBW properties of $\mathcal D_\kappa$
are proved in [[lem-pa36-flag-tdo-pbw-and-twist]]. A left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module below is required to be quasi-coherent as an
$\mathcal O_X$-module.

For $z\in Z(U(\mathfrak g))$, let $\operatorname{pr}(z)\in U(\mathfrak h)$ be
the Harish–Chandra projection along the chosen triangular decomposition, and
put
$$\chi_\kappa(z)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\kappa-\rho).$$
This is the shifted central character: the Harish–Chandra isomorphism makes it
$W$-invariant in $\kappa$. Define
$$A_\kappa=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\kappa.$$
The regularity convention is **antidominant** when
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\notin\mathbb Z_{>0}$ for each positive
root $\alpha$, and **regular** when
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ne0$ for every root. For complex weights,
$\mathbb Z_{>0}$ means the positive real integers; no order on arbitrary
complex numbers is used.

Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the
isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying
$$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$
If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$
and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ defines an equivalence between left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules and left $\mathcal D_{\kappa+\eta}$-modules.

derivations.claim: The derived algebra $[\mathfrak p_\alpha,\mathfrak p_\alpha]$ is spanned by positive-root spaces and the rank-one subalgebra $\langle\mathfrak g_\alpha,\mathfrak g_{-\alpha},\alpha^\vee\rangle$. The functional $\kappa$ vanishes on the root spaces by its definition and on $\alpha^\vee$ by the assumed zero pairing. It therefore kills the derived algebra, so it is a Lie algebra character of $\mathfrak p_\alpha$. Its transport to the isotropy bundle on $Y$ is well-defined because a character is invariant under conjugation by the connected group $P_\alpha$. Applying the PBW quotient construction of [F3] to the action algebroid of $G$ on $Y$ defines $\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$ with associated graded $\operatorname{Sym}T_Y$.

Choose a Zariski open $U\subseteq Y$ with a section $s:U\to G$ of the $P_\alpha$-torsor, as in [F2]. For a principal $H$-bundle $Q\to Z$, write its Atiyah algebroid as $T_Q/H$, the bundle of $H$-invariant vector fields with its anchor and bracket. The infinitesimal left $G$-action identifies the action algebroid of $G$ on $G/B$ with this Atiyah algebroid for $G\to X$: on each fiber the left fundamental fields identify $\mathfrak g$ with $T_gG$, and the sign convention is the one in the displayed action-algebroid bracket. The section identifies $G|_U$ with $U\times P_\alpha$, so the Borel torsor is $U\times P_\alpha\to U\times(P_\alpha/B)$. Its Atiyah algebroid splits as $T_U\oplus\operatorname{pr}_2^*\operatorname{At}(P_\alpha\to P_\alpha/B)$, with zero cross-brackets because the two factors act on separate coordinates. The action algebroid of $G$ on $Y=G/P_\alpha$ similarly becomes the Atiyah algebroid of $G\to Y$, locally $T_U\oplus(U\times\mathfrak p_\alpha)$; quotienting its isotropy by $\kappa|_{\mathfrak p_\alpha}$ leaves $\operatorname{Diff}_U$, which is the local form of $\mathcal D^\alpha_{\kappa-\rho}$. In the vertical factor $\operatorname{At}(P_\alpha\to P_\alpha/B)$, the rank-one isotropy character is zero because $\kappa$ vanishes on the root spaces and on $\alpha^\vee$; the central isotropy acts trivially on $P_\alpha/B$ and its scalar relation adds no relative differential operator. Thus the vertical quotient is the rank-one TDO with parameter $-\rho_{\mathfrak{sl}_2}$, which by [F3] is $\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1})$. The PBW normal forms of the direct-product algebroid therefore identify $$\mathcal D_{\kappa-\rho}|_{p_\alpha^{-1}(U)}\cong\mathcal D_{\mathbb P^1}\boxtimes\mathcal D^\alpha_{\kappa-\rho}|_U.$$ The line bundle $\mathcal O_X(\rho)$ restricts to degree $-1$ on the fiber because its associated character pairs to $1$ with $\alpha^\vee$; hence its restriction is $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$.

On overlaps, write the torsor sections as $s_j=s_i p_{ij}$ for a regular map $p_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to P_\alpha$. The change of product trivialization is $(u,qB)\mapsto(u,p_{ij}(u)qB)$. On the Atiyah algebroid it is the gauge transformation of the product principal $B$-bundle: its base component includes the derivative of $p_{ij}$ in $\mathfrak p_\alpha$, and its fiber component is the differential of left multiplication by $p_{ij}(u)$ on $P_\alpha/B$. The quotient of the base component by $\kappa|_{\mathfrak p_\alpha}$ is exactly the transition of $\mathcal D^\alpha_{\kappa-\rho}$; the fiber component acts by the chain rule on relative operators. The isotropy character is preserved because it is a Lie-algebra character invariant under $\operatorname{Ad}(P_\alpha)$, and the equality $p_{ik}=p_{ij}p_{jk}$ makes the gauge maps compose, giving the cocycle identity. Thus the local product TDO identifications agree on overlaps. The local ordinary inverse-image modules $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}\boxtimes N|_U$ glue to $p_\alpha^\dagger N$: in product coordinates a vertical field acts by $\partial_z(f\otimes n)=\partial_z(f)\otimes n$, and a base operator acts by its derivative on $f$ plus its given action on $n$. The chain rule is precisely the algebroid transition just checked, so this is a module for the pulled-back TDO, not its regular left module. Finally [F3] identifies $\mathcal O_X(\rho)\otimes p_\alpha^\dagger N$ as a $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module because tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\rho)$ shifts the parameter from $\kappa-\rho$ to $\kappa$.

Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the
isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying
$$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$
If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$
and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ defines an equivalence between left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules and left $\mathcal D_{\kappa+\eta}$-modules.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and Weyl group $W$,
and let $p_1,\dots,p_r$ be homogeneous basic generators of $S(\mathfrak g)^{\mathfrak g}$
of degrees $d_1,\dots,d_r$, corresponding by Chevalley restriction to basic Weyl
invariants ([[thm-symmetric-invariants-restrict-to-weyl-invariants]],
[[thm-chevalley-shephard-todd-for-finite-weyl-groups]]). Put
$$A=S(\mathfrak g)/(p_1,\dots,p_r).$$ Then $A$ is a reduced integral domain of
dimension $\dim\mathfrak g-r=2|\Phi^+|$, with Hilbert series
$$\operatorname{Hilb}(A,t)=\frac{\prod_{i=1}^r(1-t^{d_i})}{(1-t)^{\dim\mathfrak g}},$$
and for every central character $\chi:Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to\mathbb C$ the PBW
associated graded of $U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi$ is canonically
isomorphic to $A$.

Assume the setup of [[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]]
and the Axiom of Choice. Let $N\subseteq\mathfrak g$ be the nilpotent cone
with its reduced coordinate ring from
[[lem-the-nilpotent-central-fiber-is-a-reduced-integral-domain]], and let
$\mu:T^*X\to N$ be the Springer moment map. Then $N$ is normal, $\mu$ is
proper and birational, and pullback induces a graded algebra isomorphism
$$\mathbb C[N]\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T^*X,\mathcal O_{T^*X}).$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the published group and sheaf
suppliers. Let $G$ be a connected simply connected complex semisimple affine
algebraic group, $B\supseteq T$ a Borel subgroup and maximal torus,
$X=G/B$, $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}G$,
$\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}T$, and $\Phi^+$ the positive roots selected by
$B$. Write $\rho=\frac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$. All schemes are over
$\mathbb C$. For an integral weight $\eta$, $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ denotes the
$G$-equivariant line bundle $G\times^B\mathbb C_\eta$ with fiber character
$\eta$ at $eB$.

The infinitesimal $G$-action gives an anchor
$$a_X:\mathcal L_X:=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathfrak g\longrightarrow T_X,\qquad f\otimes x\longmapsto f x_X.$$
Give $\mathcal L_X$ the action-algebroid bracket
$$[f\otimes x,g\otimes y]=fg\otimes[x,y]+f x_X(g)\otimes y-g y_X(f)\otimes x.$$
Its kernel $\mathfrak b_X=\ker a_X$ is the isotropy Lie-algebra bundle; at
$gB$ its fiber is $\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak b$.

For any $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$, the character $\kappa+\rho$ of
$\mathfrak b$ (zero on $\mathfrak n^+$) transports to an
$\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\chi^X_{\kappa+\rho}:\mathfrak b_X\to\mathcal O_X$.
The transport is independent of the representative $g$ of $gB$, since a
character is invariant under the adjoint action of $B$. The action-algebroid
enveloping sheaf $\mathcal U_X(\mathfrak g)$ is generated by $\mathcal O_X$
and $\mathcal L_X$ with the displayed bracket and
$$[x,f]=x_X(f),\qquad x\in\mathcal L_X,\ f\in\mathcal O_X.$$
Define the sheaf of twisted differential operators
$$\mathcal D_\kappa:=\mathcal U_X(\mathfrak g)/\bigl(\xi-\chi^X_{\kappa+\rho}(\xi):\xi\in\mathfrak b_X\bigr).$$
Its order filtration assigns order zero to $\mathcal O_X$ and order at most
one to the image of $\mathcal L_X$. A TDO means a filtered
$\mathcal O_X$-ring with $F_0=\mathcal O_X$, associated graded
$\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X$, and first-order commutator equal to
the anchor; the well-definedness and PBW properties of $\mathcal D_\kappa$
are proved in [[lem-pa36-flag-tdo-pbw-and-twist]]. A left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module below is required to be quasi-coherent as an
$\mathcal O_X$-module.

For $z\in Z(U(\mathfrak g))$, let $\operatorname{pr}(z)\in U(\mathfrak h)$ be
the Harish–Chandra projection along the chosen triangular decomposition, and
put
$$\chi_\kappa(z)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\kappa-\rho).$$
This is the shifted central character: the Harish–Chandra isomorphism makes it
$W$-invariant in $\kappa$. Define
$$A_\kappa=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\kappa.$$
The regularity convention is **antidominant** when
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\notin\mathbb Z_{>0}$ for each positive
root $\alpha$, and **regular** when
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ne0$ for every root. For complex weights,
$\mathbb Z_{>0}$ means the positive real integers; no order on arbitrary
complex numbers is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be the connected simply connected complex
semisimple affine algebraic group with Borel $B=T\ltimes U$, positive roots
$\Phi^+$ and flag variety $X=G/B$ of
[[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]] and
[[lem-semisimple-borel-root-factorization]], let
$$\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\beta\in\Phi^+}\beta$$
be the Weyl vector of the chosen positive system, so that
$2\rho=\sum_{\beta\in\Phi^+}\beta$ is the sum of the positive roots
([[def-weyl-vector-rho]]), and let
$$\mathcal L_\lambda=G\times^B\mathbb C_{-\lambda}$$
be the Borel-character equivariant line bundle of
[[def-borel-character-equivariant-line-bundle]]. Then the canonical line
bundle (dualizing line bundle)
$$\omega_X=\det\Omega^1_{X/\mathbb C}=\textstyle\bigwedge^{|\Phi^+|}\Omega^1_{X/\mathbb C}$$
of [[def-smooth-projective-dualizing-line-bundle-and-trace]] is isomorphic to
$\mathcal L_{-2\rho}$: the canonical line of the flag variety is the
equivariant line bundle attached to the character $-2\rho$. With the fibre
conventions of [[def-borel-character-equivariant-line-bundle]], the fibre at
$eB$ of both sides is the one-dimensional $B$-module $\mathbb C_{2\rho}$.

Let $M$ be a cyclic highest-weight module with highest vector $v$ of weight $\lambda$, and let $z\in Z(U(\mathfrak g))$. Then

$$zv=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\lambda)\,v,$$

so the scalar by which $z$ acts on $M$ is obtained by evaluating the Harish-Chandra projection at $\lambda$.

derivations.claim: Let $\phi_\kappa:U(\mathfrak g)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal D_\kappa)$ be the infinitesimal-action map. Use the fiber $Q=\mathcal D_{\kappa,eB}/\mathcal D_{\kappa,eB}\mathfrak m_{eB}$ for the right $\mathcal O_X$-module structure, and write $\delta$ for the class of $1$. This is a left $U(\mathfrak g)$-module. Choose local coordinates $t_j$ at $eB$ and a local differential-operator trivialization. For $b\in\mathfrak b$, its operator is $\sum_j f_j\partial_{t_j}+c_b$, with $f_j(eB)=0$ and $c_b(eB)=(\kappa+\rho)(b)$ by the isotropy relation. Moving coefficients to the right gives $b\delta=(c_b(eB)-\sum_j\partial_{t_j}f_j(eB))\delta$. The anchor action on functions is the negative of the tangent action on points, so its linear trace on $\mathfrak g/\mathfrak b$ is $2\rho(b)$, since the tangent weights are the negative roots; equivalently this is the canonical character in [F4]. Thus $b\delta=(\kappa-\rho)(b)\delta$, and $\mathfrak n^+\delta=0$. Negative-root vector fields span the tangent space at $eB$; PBW symbols [F1] show that their ordered monomials on $\delta$ span $Q$ by induction on order. Hence $Q$ is a cyclic highest-weight module of weight $\kappa-\rho$, so every central $z$ acts by $\operatorname{pr}(z)(\kappa-\rho)=\chi_\kappa(z)$ by [F5]. Equivariance gives the same scalar on every closed right fiber. Only Lie algebra characters were used, so no nonintegral line bundle is required.

Fix an order bound $m$. The space $U(\mathfrak g)_{\le m}$ is finite-dimensional by PBW, and $F_m\mathcal D_\kappa$ is locally free of finite rank as a right $\mathcal O_X$-module by the same PBW normal forms [F1]. For $z\in\ker\chi_\kappa$, the right $\mathcal O_X$-linear multiplication map $U(\mathfrak g)_{\le m}\otimes\mathcal O_X\to F_{m+d(z)}\mathcal D_\kappa$ given by $u\otimes f\mapsto\phi_\kappa(u(z-\chi_\kappa(z)))f$ is zero on every closed fiber by step 1.1. In local frames this is a finite matrix of regular functions vanishing at every closed point; $X$ is reduced and of finite type over $\mathbb C$, so each entry is zero. Thus $\phi_\kappa$ kills the whole two-sided central ideal and factors through a filtered map $\bar\phi_\kappa:A_\kappa\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal D_\kappa)$. This finite-rank argument does not apply Nakayama to an infinitely generated module.

The associated-graded map fits into $$\mathbb C[N]\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}A_\kappa \longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}\Gamma(X,\mathcal D_\kappa) \hookrightarrow\Gamma(X,\operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa) =\Gamma(T^*X,\mathcal O).$$ The last inclusion follows by applying the left-exact functor $\Gamma$ to each order-filtration sequence. The composite is pullback by the Springer moment map: for $x\in\mathfrak g$, its linear function on $N$ pulls back to the principal symbol of the vector field $x_X$, namely $\xi\mapsto\xi(x_X)$ on $T^*X$. Linear functions generate $\mathbb C[N]$ as a quotient of $S(\mathfrak g)$, so the two algebra maps agree on all generators. By [F3] the composite is an isomorphism.

Since the composite in [step 3.1] is an isomorphism and its right-hand map is injective, both intermediate associated-graded maps are isomorphisms. A filtered map with associated-graded isomorphism is an isomorphism: lift a target symbol and subtract a lift to lower the order until surjectivity holds; for injectivity, a nonzero kernel element would have a nonzero leading symbol in the graded kernel. Hence $\bar\phi_\kappa$ is the asserted filtered algebra isomorphism. The argument uses no order condition on $\kappa$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\lambda\in X^*(T)$.
If $\lambda$ is not dominant integral then $H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$. If
$\lambda$ is dominant integral then
$H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)\cong L(\lambda)^*$ as $\mathfrak g$-modules, and
$H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$ for every $i>0$.

Let $G$ be a complex affine algebraic group acting algebraically on a classical complex variety $X$ ([[def-rational-action-on-affine-variety]], [[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), and let $L$ be an invertible sheaf on $X$ with total space $p:L\to X$ ([[def-invertible-sheaf]]), the total space being obtained by gluing $U\times\mathbb A^1$ over local frames of $L$ using their invertible regular transition functions, and the projection being a morphism of locally ringed spaces ([[def-morphism-locally-ringed-spaces]]). Write $\sigma:G\times X\to X$ for the action.

A **$G$-linearization** of $L$ is an algebraic $G$-action $m:G\times L\to L$ on the total space such that

- $p(m(g,\ell))=g\,p(\ell)$ for all $g\in G$, $\ell\in L$, and
- for every $g\in G$ and $x\in X$ the fibre map $L_x\to L_{gx}$, $\ell\mapsto g\ell$, is $\mathbb C$-linear.

A **$G$-linearized invertible sheaf** is an invertible sheaf together with a linearization; the pair is written $(L,m)$. Equivalently, a linearization is an isomorphism $\varphi:\sigma^*L\to \mathrm{pr}_2^*L$ of sheaves on $G\times X$ satisfying the cocycle identity

$$\mathrm{pr}_{23}^*\varphi\circ(\mathrm{id}_G\times\sigma)^*\varphi=(m_G\times\mathrm{id}_X)^*\varphi,$$

where $m_G:G\times G\to G$ is the multiplication; at $(g,h,x)$ both sides map the fibre $L_{ghx}$ to $L_x$. The isomorphism $\varphi$ sends a vector over $gx$ to its translate by $g^{-1}$ over $x$, so its inverse recovers the action on total spaces.

For any algebraic character $\chi:G\to\mathbf G_m=\mathbb C^\times$ the **twist** $(L,m)_\chi$ multiplies the fibre action by $\chi(g)$ and is again a linearization of the same invertible sheaf. In particular linearizations are not unique, the trivial action admits the trivial linearization of $\mathcal O_X$ and its twists, and for a finite-dimensional rational $G$-module $V$ the induced action on the tautological line bundle linearizes $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P(V)}(-1)$, and its dual linearizes $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P(V)}(1)$.

The two main theorems of this page always assume that a linearization is given; no general existence of linearizations is claimed here.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\lambda\in X^*(T)$.
If $\lambda$ is not dominant integral then $H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$. If
$\lambda$ is dominant integral then
$H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)\cong L(\lambda)^*$ as $\mathfrak g$-modules, and
$H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$ for every $i>0$.

Let $E$ be the real span of a finite reduced crystallographic root system
$\Phi$, with chosen positive roots $\Phi^+$, simple roots
$\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r\}$, Weyl group $W$ and root lattice
$Q=\sum_i\mathbb Z\alpha_i$. Extend the pairing complex linearly to
$E_\mathbb C$. For $\kappa\in E_\mathbb C$, call $\kappa$ antidominant if
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\notin\mathbb Z_{>0}$ for every
$\alpha\in\Phi^+$, and regular if
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ne0$ for every root. Then
$$\kappa-w\kappa\notin Q_+\setminus\{0\}\qquad(w\in W)$$
for antidominant $\kappa$, and
$$\kappa-w\kappa\notin Q_+\qquad(w\ne1)$$
when $\kappa$ is also regular. Here
$Q_+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$.

Assume the setup of [[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]] and the Axiom of
Choice. For every complex $\kappa$, the infinitesimal action on
$\mathcal D_\kappa$ induces a filtered algebra isomorphism
$$A_\kappa=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\kappa \xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X,\mathcal D_\kappa),$$
where $\chi_\kappa(z)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\kappa-\rho)$. No dominance,
regularity, or integrality condition is imposed on $\kappa$.

Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the
isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying
$$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$
If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$
and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ defines an equivalence between left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules and left $\mathcal D_{\kappa+\eta}$-modules.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $I_1,\ldots,I_r$ be pairwise comaximal ideals, where $r\ge1$. Then the canonical map
$$ R\longrightarrow \prod_{i=1}^r R/I_i,\qquad x\longmapsto(x+I_1,\ldots,x+I_r) $$
is surjective, its kernel is $\bigcap_{i=1}^r I_i$, and
$$ \bigcap_{i=1}^r I_i=\prod_{i=1}^r I_i. $$
Equivalently,
$$ R/\prod_{i=1}^r I_i\cong\prod_{i=1}^r R/I_i. $$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra, let $\mathfrak h$ be any Cartan subalgebra in the
nilpotent self-normalizing sense, and fix a positive root system with Weyl
group $W$ and half-sum $\rho$ of its positive roots. The shifted Harish-Chandra map

$$ \operatorname{HC}_\rho\colon Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to S(\mathfrak h)^W, \qquad \operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)(\lambda)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\lambda-\rho), $$

is an algebra isomorphism.

derivations.claim: Form the finite $G$-equivariant bundle $E(V_\eta)=G\times^B V_\eta$. The map $[g,v]\mapsto(gB,gv)$ identifies it with the trivial bundle $X\times V_\eta$ with its diagonal $G$-action. Choose a weight basis in each weight space and order the weights with higher weights first. Positive root operators raise weights, so the resulting complete filtration is $B$-stable and its successive quotient lines have characters $\eta_j$ as in [F2]. Association to $G\to X$ is exact on this finite filtration: on every torsor chart it is tensoring a sequence of complex vector spaces with $\mathcal O_X$. Its quotient line bundles are $\mathcal O_X(\eta_j)$, with highest line $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$. Tensoring this bundle filtration with arbitrary $M$ remains exact, since each quotient is locally free.

The coevaluation $\mathcal O_X\to L_\eta\otimes E(V_\eta)$ is the highest line in this filtration; dually the evaluation $E(V_\eta)^*\to L_\eta$ is the quotient of weight $-\eta$. These are the duals of evaluation of the globally generated line bundle [F1], so they are respectively injective and surjective, locally split as vector-bundle maps. After tensoring with $M$ they give the maps in the Statement, with the same exact filtration positions. Each associated quotient of the first target is $M\otimes\mathcal O_X(-\eta+\eta_j)$, with central character $\chi_{\kappa-\eta+\eta_j}$ by [F4]. The evaluation source has quotients $M\otimes\mathcal O_X(-\eta_j)$ with characters $\chi_{\kappa-\eta_j}$; its target has character $\chi_{\kappa-\eta}$. All these filtrations are preserved by the diagonal $\mathfrak g$-action because their finite bundle factors are $G$-equivariant.

For the coevaluation, every quotient other than its image has $\eta_j\ne\eta$. If its character were $\chi_\kappa$, equality of Harish–Chandra characters would give some $w\in W$ with $\kappa-w\kappa=\eta-\eta_j\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$, contrary to [F3]. Thus the image is the sole filtration quotient with character $\chi_\kappa$. This argument applies to the actual filtered module involving $M$, not to a supposed tensor-character identity for an unfiltered arbitrary tensor product.

For the evaluation, if $\eta_j\ne\eta$ had $\chi_{\kappa-\eta_j}=\chi_{\kappa-\eta}$, then $\kappa-\eta_j=w(\kappa-\eta)$ for some $w$. Rearranging gives $\kappa-w^{-1}\kappa=\eta-w^{-1}\eta_j\in Q_+$, since $w^{-1}\eta_j$ is again a weight of $V_\eta$. If the right side is nonzero, antidominance [F3] rules it out; if it is zero, regularity [F3] forces $w=1$ and hence $\eta_j=\eta$, a contradiction. Thus its target is the sole quotient with the distinguished character.

For a sheaf of complex vector spaces with a finite filtration of exact central-character quotients, a product of powers of their finitely many maximal ideals in $Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ annihilates the sheaf. Powers of distinct maximal ideals are comaximal: expand $1=(u+v)^{a+b-1}$ with $u+v=1$, $u$ in the first ideal and $v$ in the second. Thus [F5] gives central polynomial projectors onto the corresponding generalized-character summands. These polynomials act on sections by the diagonal differential $U(\mathfrak g)$-action, commute with restrictions and with $U(\mathfrak g)$, and hence are morphisms of sheaves of complex vector spaces. They are natural in $M$. They are generally differential operators rather than $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps; that stronger linearity is neither asserted nor needed.

By step 3.1 the distinguished projector on the coevaluation target has image exactly the injected copy of $M$: it is identity on that copy, and its induced action on the filtered quotient is zero. Composing with the inverse of this identification gives a sheaf retraction. By step 3.2 the distinguished summand of the evaluation source maps isomorphically onto its target, since the kernel has no such character; invert that restriction to get its sheaf section. Step 3.3 supplies all asserted naturality and $U(\mathfrak g)$-linearity. Applying sheaf cohomology to either split pair preserves its retraction or section, proving the final assertion.

Choice. For every complex $\kappa$, the infinitesimal action on

$$A_\kappa=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\kappa \xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X,\mathcal D_\kappa),$$
where $\chi_\kappa(z)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\kappa-\rho)$. No dominance,
regularity, or integrality condition is imposed on $\kappa$.

Fix $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ and $A_\kappa$, $\mathcal D_\kappa$ as in
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. By
[[thm-pa36-global-twisted-differential-operators]], the sheaf
$\mathcal D_\kappa$ is a right $A_\kappa$-module by multiplication by global
sections, and $\Gamma(X,-)$ takes values in left $A_\kappa$-modules through
the infinitesimal action. Define
$$\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa(V):=\mathcal D_\kappa\otimes_{A_\kappa}V, \qquad V\in A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod},$$
where the tensor product is the sheaf tensor product. Define
$\Gamma_\kappa(M):=\Gamma(X,M)$ for a quasi-coherent left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$. Localization is right exact as a tensor
functor. The next item proves the adjunction and verifies that these
constructions land in the stated categories.

Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the
isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying
$$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$
If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$

auxiliary_proof_evidence.quote: Work on a Zariski open set where $T_X$ and $\mathfrak b_X$ are free and the anchor splits as an $\mathcal O_X$-module map. Combine tangent lifts $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ and a frame $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ of $\mathfrak b_X$ into one frame $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of the full action algebroid, ordered with the tangent lifts first and the isotropy frame last. For every frame generator use the relations $e_a f=f e_a+a(e_a)(f)$ and, for $b>a$, $e_b e_a=e_a e_b+[e_b,e_a]$ to move functions left and order all generators; write each bracket in the chosen frame with its local function coefficients. Reordering terminates by lexicographic induction on generator degree, the number of generator/function inversions (a generator to the left of a coefficient), and the inversion count of the frame-generator word. A commutator correction lowers generator degree; the leading function move lowers the second count, and an out-of-order generator swap lowers the third. The only overlap types are $e_a(fg)$, $e_b e_a f$, and $e_c e_b e_a$ for arbitrary frame indices, including isotropy indices. Their reductions agree by the derivation rule for the anchor, the anchor identity $a([e_b,e_a])=[a(e_b),a(e_a)]$, and Jacobi for the action-algebroid bracket [F2]. A terminating rewriting system with every such overlap resolved has unique normal forms: induction on maximum remaining reduction length joins any two first reductions at their common overlap, after which induction identifies the normal forms. Hence the ordered monomials in all $e_a$, with coefficients on the left, form a local $\mathcal O_X$-basis, and the indicated ordering puts every tangent-lift monomial before isotropy monomials. Their leading symbols are the corresponding symmetric monomials, proving $\operatorname{gr}\mathcal U_X(\mathfrak g)\cong \operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X\otimes\mathfrak g)$. [F1, F2, algebra, construct]

On a chart pulled back to $G$, the isotropy character is the constant $B$-character $\kappa+\rho$. It kills $[\mathfrak b,\mathfrak b]$ and is invariant under $B$-conjugation; equivariance therefore gives $\chi^X([x,\xi])=a(x)(\chi^X(\xi))$ for every local algebroid section $x$ and isotropy section $\xi$. In the ordered forms of step 1.1, use $b_a=\chi^X(b_a)$ to eliminate each isotropy generator. The overlaps of this elimination with two isotropy generators agree because $\chi^X$ kills their bracket; the overlaps with a tangent lift agree by the displayed invariance identity; and overlaps with functions agree because $a(b_a)=0$. Thus the quotient has the ordered tangent-lift monomials as a local basis, and its associated graded is $$\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X\otimes\mathfrak g)/ (\mathfrak b_X)\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$ The degree-zero part is $\mathcal O_X$, and the first-order commutator is the anchor inherited from $\mathcal U_X(\mathfrak g)$. This proves the TDO axioms and the two-sidedness of the defining ideal. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra, construct]

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let
$\operatorname{Mod}_A$ be the category of $A$-modules and
$\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ the full subcategory of $\mathcal O_X$-modules
consisting of the quasi-coherent ones ([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]).

Consider the functors
$$(-)^{\sim}:\operatorname{Mod}_A\longrightarrow\operatorname{QCoh}(X),\qquad M\longmapsto\widetilde M,$$
given by the associated module sheaf
([[def-associated-sheaf-module-affine-scheme]],
[[thm-associated-module-sheaf-exists]]), and
$$\Gamma(X,-):\operatorname{QCoh}(X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}_A,\qquad \mathcal F\longmapsto\Gamma(X,\mathcal F).$$

Then:

1. For every $A$-module $M$ the canonical map
   $M\to\Gamma(X,\widetilde M)$, $m\mapsto m$ (the section over $X$), is an
   isomorphism of $A$-modules ([[lem-associated-sheaf-sections-basic-open]]).
2. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ the canonical comparison morphism
   $\kappa_{\mathcal F}:\widetilde{\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)}\to\mathcal F$,
   whose component on $D(f)$ is the localisation at $f$ of the restriction map
   $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\mathcal F(D(f))$, is an isomorphism of
   $\mathcal O_X$-modules. In particular
   $\mathcal F\cong\widetilde{\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)}$.
3. $(-)^{\sim}$ is fully faithful: for all $A$-modules $M,N$ the map
   $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\widetilde M,\widetilde N)$,
   $u\mapsto\widetilde u$, is a bijection, with inverse
   $\psi\mapsto\psi_X$.
4. Consequently $(-)^{\sim}$ and $\Gamma(X,-)$ are quasi-inverse equivalences
   $\operatorname{Mod}_A\simeq\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$: the unit in (1) and the
   counit in (2) are natural isomorphisms, and $M\mapsto\widetilde M$ is an
   equivalence of categories.

All claims include the zero ring $A=0$, where $X=\varnothing$, both categories
are equivalent to the terminal category, and the assertions are trivial. The
Axiom of Choice is used only as it is used by the associated-sheaf existence
theorem and its consequences cited below, and by the compactness of
$\operatorname{Spec}A$.

derivations.claim: On an affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, put $Q=\Gamma(U,\mathcal D_\kappa)$. Right multiplication by $A_\kappa$ commutes with left multiplication by $R$. Thus $Q\otimes_{A_\kappa}V$ is an $R$-module, and for every $f\in R$ there is a natural isomorphism $$Q_f\otimes_{A_\kappa}V\cong(Q\otimes_{A_\kappa}V)_f,\qquad(q/f^m)\otimes v\longmapsto(q\otimes v)/f^m.$$ The inverse sends $(q\otimes v)/f^m$ to $(q/f^m)\otimes v$; additivity and the balancing relations make both maps well-defined. By [F2] and [F3], the tensor presheaf on the distinguished-open basis of $U$ is therefore the associated sheaf of $Q\otimes_{A_\kappa}V$. Its sheafification has that restriction on $U$, proving that $\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa V$ is quasi-coherent. Left multiplication on its first factor gives its left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-action.

The tensor-Hom correspondence here follows directly from balancing. Given an $A_\kappa$-linear map $V\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_\kappa}(\mathcal D_\kappa,M)$, write its value at $v$ as $h_v$ and send $d\otimes v$ over $W$ to $h_v|_W(d)$. The $A_\kappa$-action on Hom is $(a h)(d)=h(da)$, so the rule is balanced, respects restrictions, and extends through sheafification to a $\mathcal D_\kappa$-linear map. Conversely such a sheaf map gives $h_v$ by $d\mapsto\phi(d\otimes v)$. These constructions are inverse and natural, and step 1.1 places their source in the required quasi-coherent category.

Evaluation at $1$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_\kappa}(\mathcal D_\kappa,M)$ with $\Gamma(X,M)$. A morphism is determined by the image of $1$; conversely, each global section $m$ defines the morphism $d\mapsto d\,m$. Under this identification the $A_\kappa$-action is the one from [F1]. Substituting into step 2.1 gives the natural bijection $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_\kappa}(\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa V,M) \cong\operatorname{Hom}_{A_\kappa}(V,\Gamma_\kappa M),$$ which is the asserted adjunction. Right exactness of localization follows because a left adjoint preserves cokernels.

Let $X$ be a scheme and let $F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module, for instance a
quasi-coherent sheaf ([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]). The **evaluation
map** of $F$ is the morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules
$$\operatorname{ev}_F:\Gamma(X,F)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathcal O_X \longrightarrow F,\qquad f\otimes g\longmapsto g\cdot f|_U\ \text{ on } U\subseteq X,$$ where the tensor product is taken over $\mathbb Z$ because the global sections $\Gamma(X,F)$ are only an abelian group in general and the sheaf $\mathcal O_X$ carries the $\mathcal O_X$-module structure. Concretely, on an open $U$ the map sends a finite sum $\sum_i f_i\otimes g_i$ with $f_i\in\Gamma(X,F)$, $g_i\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ to $\sum_i g_i\cdot f_i|_U$. The sheaf $F$ is **globally generated** when $\operatorname{ev}_F$ is surjective. Equivalently, for every point $x\in X$ the images of the global sections generate the stalk $F_x$ as an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module: passing to stalks, $(\operatorname{ev}_F)_x$ is the map $\Gamma(X,F)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to F_x$, and a morphism of sheaves is surjective exactly when it is surjective on every stalk. For an **invertible** sheaf $L$ the condition takes the following form ([[def-invertible-sheaf]]): if there are finitely many global sections $s_0,\dots,s_n\in\Gamma(X,L)$ such that the induced morphism $$\mathcal O_X^{\,n+1}\longrightarrow L,\qquad (g_0,\dots,g_n)\longmapsto \sum_i g_i s_i,$$ is surjective, then $L$ is globally generated, since this morphism factors the evaluation map. $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$, the natural coevaluation map
$$M\longrightarrow M\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}L_\eta\otimes_{\mathbb C}V_\eta$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be the connected simply connected complex
semisimple affine algebraic group with Borel $B=T\ltimes U$ and Weyl group $W$
of [[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]] and
[[lem-semisimple-borel-root-factorization]], and let $\alpha$ be a simple
root with minimal parabolic $P_\alpha=B\sqcup Bn_\alpha B$, root subgroup
$U_{-\alpha}$ and Weyl subgroup $\{1,s_\alpha\}$ as in
[[lem-semisimple-minimal-parabolic-root-subgroup]]. Let
$\pi_B:G\to X_B$ and $\pi_\alpha:G\to X_\alpha$ be the orbit maps of
[[lem-semisimple-projective-orbit-flag-quotients]]. Then:

(i) the induced map $f:X_B\to X_\alpha$, $g[v_B]\mapsto g[v_\alpha]$, is a
surjective morphism of varieties, well defined because $B\subseteq P_\alpha$,
and its fibre over $g[v_\alpha]$ is canonically the coset space
$P_\alpha/B$, which is $\mathbb P^1$ in the two-chart description
$z\mapsto u_{-\alpha}(z)B$, $t\mapsto u_\alpha(t)n_\alpha B$ with $t=z^{-1}$
of [[lem-semisimple-minimal-parabolic-root-subgroup]];

(ii) $f$ is a Zariski-locally trivial fibre bundle with fibre $\mathbb P^1$: over each single $G$-translate $gV$ of the open torsor chart $V=\sigma_\alpha(U^-_\alpha)\subseteq X_\alpha$ from [[lem-semisimple-flag-torsor-zariski-charts]], it becomes the projection $gV\times\mathbb P^1\to gV$. These translates cover $X_\alpha$ and admit a finite subcover. In the rank-one case $G=P_\alpha$, the base is a point and $f$ is the unique map from $\mathbb P^1$ to that point.

Let $\alpha$ be a simple root, $P_\alpha$ its minimal parabolic,
$Y=G/P_\alpha$, and $p_\alpha:X=G/B\to Y$. Let
$\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ satisfy $\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$.
The restriction of $\kappa$ to $\mathfrak p_\alpha$ that is zero on root
spaces is a Lie algebra character. Define the partial-flag TDO
$\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$ on $Y$ as the action-algebroid quotient
whose isotropy character is this restriction of $\kappa$; the subscript
$\kappa-\rho$ uses the convention that a TDO parameter $\nu$ has isotropy
character $\nu+\rho$. For a quasicoherent left
$\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$-module $N$, define $p_\alpha^\dagger N$
on a Zariski product chart $p_\alpha^{-1}(U)\cong U\times\mathbb P^1$ to be
the ordinary inverse-image module $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}\boxtimes N|_U$: relative vector fields differentiate the first factor, and base operators act on the second. Its underlying sheaf is $\mathcal O_X\otimes_{p_\alpha^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}p_\alpha^{-1}N$; the differential transition maps are induced by the chain rule under changes of the $P_\alpha$-torsor section. Then
these local modules glue to a quasicoherent left
$\mathcal D_{\kappa-\rho}$-module, and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\rho)$
turns it into a left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module. The restriction of
$\mathcal O_X(\rho)$ to each $p_\alpha$-fiber is
$\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$.

For a torsor section $s:U\to G$, the product chart used below is the
commutative square whose top arrow is $\Phi_s(u,qB)=s(u)qB$:

```tikzcd
U\times P_\alpha/B \arrow[r,"\Phi_s"] \arrow[d,"\mathrm{pr}_1"'] & p_\alpha^{-1}(U) \arrow[d,"p_\alpha"] \\
U \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}_U"'] & U
```

The left vertical map is projection, and the bottom map is identity. The
torsor section makes $\Phi_s$ an isomorphism; the equality
$p_\alpha\circ\Phi_s=\mathrm{pr}_1$ verifies commutativity. The diagram
records the local chart only; the PBW and gluing arguments below prove the
TDO identifications.

Assume the complex flag-variety setup, including the Axiom of Choice, of
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. On $Z=\mathbb P^1$ put
$L=\mathcal O_Z(-1)$, $D=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_Z)$ and
$D_0=\operatorname{Diff}(L)$. Form $E=D_0\otimes_{\mathcal O_Z}L$, using
the right $\mathcal O_Z$-action on $D_0$. Evaluation gives
$$E/D_0\Gamma(Z,E)\cong L.$$
Every quasi-coherent $D_0$-module $Q$ with $\Gamma(Z,Q)=0$ has the canonical
form
$$Q\cong L\otimes_{\mathbb C}\Gamma(Z,L^{-1}\otimes Q),$$
with trivial $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action on the second factor.

For any commutative $\mathbb C$-algebra $R$, the same classification holds
for quasi-coherent modules over the vertical ring $D_{0,R}$ on
$\mathbb P^1_R$: its kernel modules are exactly
$L_R\otimes_R N$ for $R$-modules $N$. This form commutes with every scalar
extension $R\to R'$. If $R$ is noetherian, coherence over $D_{0,R}$ is
equivalent to finite generation of $N$ over $R$. Scalar extension here
concerns only the vertical ring and a central base ring; it makes no claim
about transporting arbitrary base derivations.

More generally let $U$ be a smooth affine complex variety and let $A$ be a
TDO on $U$. For the projection $r:Z\times U\to U$, a coherent
$(D_0\boxtimes A)$-module $Q$ satisfies $R^q r_*Q=0$ for $q>0$; moreover
$r_*Q=0$ if and only if the evaluation isomorphism is
$$Q\cong L\boxtimes N,\qquad N=r_*(L^{-1}\otimes Q),$$
where $N$ is a unique coherent $A$-module. Here the ordinary differential
inverse image has underlying sheaf $\mathcal O_Z\boxtimes N$ and relative
vector fields differentiate its $\mathcal O_Z$ factor. These isomorphisms
are natural in all commuting base differential operators. Consequently they
glue over locally trivial $\mathbb P^1$-bundles with compatible product TDO
charts and line bundle restricting to $L$, as in
[[lem-pa36-partial-flag-twist-product]].

derivations.claim: Since $\Gamma_\kappa$ is exact, its kernel $K$ is closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions; hence $K$ is a Serre subcategory. The functor $\Gamma_\kappa$ therefore descends to the Serre quotient.

Localization is right exact. For a short exact sequence $0\to V'\to V\to V''\to0$ of $A_\kappa$-modules, applying localization gives a right-exact sequence $$\operatorname{Loc}V'\longrightarrow\operatorname{Loc}V \longrightarrow\operatorname{Loc}V''\longrightarrow0.$$ Apply the exact functor $\Gamma_\kappa$ and use [F2]. The resulting sequence is $0\to V'\to V\to V''\to0$. Therefore the kernel of $\operatorname{Loc}V'\to\operatorname{Loc}V$ has zero global sections and lies in $K$. Thus localization becomes exact after passage to the Serre quotient.

The unit is an isomorphism by [F2], so it remains an isomorphism in the quotient. For any $M$, the triangular identity in [F3] shows that applying $\Gamma_\kappa$ to the counit $\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa\Gamma_\kappa M\to M$ gives an isomorphism. By exactness [F1], the kernel and cokernel of the counit lie in $K$; hence the counit is an isomorphism in the quotient. The descended unit and counit prove the claimed equivalence.

For an arbitrary $M$, let $E$ be the image of the counit $\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa\Gamma M\to M$. By step 3.1 its cokernel has zero global sections, so $E$ and $M$ define isomorphic objects of the Serre quotient. The source is generated by its global sections, hence so is $E$. This holds even for generation as an $\mathcal O_X$-module: PBW and the surjective action anchor show that $\mathcal D_\kappa$ is locally spanned over $\mathcal O_X$ by products of the global $\mathfrak g$-operators; their actions on global sections remain global sections. Among the submodules of $E$ with zero global sections, take their sum $T$. This is a set-indexed sum: a submodule sheaf is specified by a family of subsets of the sets $E(U)$, one for each open $U\subseteq X$. The direct sum of any such family is again a quasicoherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module, and $\Gamma$ commutes with it by [F4]. Exactness of $\Gamma$ [F1] then gives $\Gamma T=0$, so $T$ is the largest submodule of $E$ in $K$. The quotient $E/T$ remains generated by global sections. If $S\subseteq E/T$ has $\Gamma S=0$, its inverse image $P\subseteq E$ fits into $0\to T\to P\to S\to0$; exactness [F1] gives $\Gamma P=0$, so $P\subseteq T$ by maximality and $S=0$. Thus $E/T$ is a representative of the same quotient object, is generated by global sections, and has no nonzero submodule in $K$. Conversely, every module with those two properties is by definition such a representative.

These representatives give an actual equivalence with the algebra-module category, not just a choice of quotient objects. If $E,D$ are generated by global sections and have no nonzero subobject in $K$, any map with zero global sections has image in $K$ and hence is zero. Given $h:\Gamma E\to\Gamma D$, adjunction [F3] gives $f:\operatorname{Loc}\Gamma E\to D$. The evaluation counit onto $E$ is surjective because $E$ is generated by global sections; its kernel is in $K$ by step 3.1. Its image under $f$ is therefore a $K$-subobject of $D$ and is zero, so $f$ factors uniquely through a map $E\to D$ inducing $h$. This proves full faithfulness of $\Gamma$ on these representatives. For any algebra module $V$, apply the construction of step 4.1 to $\operatorname{Loc}V$; [F1]–[F2] give its representative global sections equal to $V$, proving essential surjectivity.

Since $\eta$ is an isomorphism, $\Gamma(\epsilon_M)$ is an isomorphism.

Exactness of $\Gamma$ in [F3] implies $\Gamma(\ker\epsilon_M)=0$ and $\Gamma(\operatorname{coker}\epsilon_M)=0$. Conservativity in [F3] makes both sheaves zero, so $\epsilon_M$ is an isomorphism. The unit and counit are isomorphisms, hence the adjoint functors are inverse equivalences.

By [[lem-enveloping-algebra-is-left-and-right-noetherian]], $U(\mathfrak g)$ is left Noetherian, so its quotient $A_\kappa$ is left Noetherian. On a smooth affine chart of $X$, $\operatorname{Sym}T_X$ is a polynomial algebra over a finite-type $\mathbb C$-algebra and hence is Noetherian by [[cor-finite-variable-polynomial-ring-noetherian]]. If a filtered ring has Noetherian associated graded, every left ideal is finitely generated: choose finitely many lifts of homogeneous generators of its graded ideal, subtract their leading terms from an arbitrary ideal element, and induct on its finite filtration degree. This proves that $\mathcal D_\kappa$ is locally left Noetherian. A finitely generated $A_\kappa$-module has a finite presentation over the Noetherian ring $A_\kappa$; localization presents it locally as a quotient of a finite free $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module, hence as a coherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module.

Let $W$ be the Weyl group of [[def-root-reflections-and-the-weyl-group-action]] and let $\rho$ be the Weyl vector of [[def-weyl-vector-rho-for-a-chosen-positive-system]]; for $w\in W$ set $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

The **BGG category $\mathcal O$** is the full subcategory of left $U(\mathfrak g)$-modules $M$ satisfying all three conditions: $M$ is finitely generated; $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathfrak h^*}M_\mu$ where $M_\mu=\{v:hv=\mu(h)v\text{ for all }h\in\mathfrak h\}$; and $U(\mathfrak n^+)v$ is finite dimensional for each $v\in M$. Its morphisms are all $\mathfrak g$-linear maps. The zero module is included, generated by the empty set. The enveloping and triangular conventions are those of [[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]] and [[thm-triangular-decomposition-from-a-chosen-positive-root-system]].

Assume the setup of [[def-pa36-global-sections-and-localization]]. If
$\kappa$ is regular antidominant, then
$$\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa:A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod} \rightleftarrows\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa):\Gamma_\kappa$$
are inverse equivalences between all left $A_\kappa$-modules and all
quasi-coherent left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules. The equivalence restricts to
finitely generated $A_\kappa$-modules and coherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules.
It does not assert that $\Gamma$ is faithful for a fixed non-antidominant
representative of a regular central character. Here a coherent
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module means a module locally finitely presented over the
sheaf of rings $\mathcal D_\kappa$; its local noetherianity is part of the
proof below.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be the connected simply connected complex
semisimple affine algebraic group with maximal torus $T$, root system $\Phi$ and
positive system $\Phi^+$ fixed in
[[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]], and for
$\alpha\in\Phi^+$ let $u_\alpha:\mathbb G_a\to U_\alpha$ be the root subgroup
constructed in [[lem-semisimple-root-exponential-algebraic-subgroups]]. Fix a
total order $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_m$ of $\Phi^+$ compatible with heights, that
is $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha_i)\le\operatorname{ht}(\alpha_j)$ whenever $i<j$.

Then the following hold.

(i) The product map
$$\prod_{i=1}^mU_{\alpha_i}\longrightarrow G,\qquad (g_1,\dots,g_m)\longmapsto g_1g_2\cdots g_m,$$
is an isomorphism of varieties onto a closed connected unipotent subgroup
$U\subseteq G$ with $\operatorname{Lie}U=\mathfrak n^+$ and $\dim U=|\Phi^+|$;
explicitly $(z_1,\dots,z_m)\mapsto u_{\alpha_1}(z_1)\cdots u_{\alpha_m}(z_m)$
is an isomorphism $\mathbb A^m\to U$ whose inverse is polynomial. The same
statements hold for every order of $\Phi^+$ compatible with heights.

(ii) $U$ is normalized by $T$, $T\cap U=1$, and
$B=T\cdot U=T\ltimes U$ is a closed connected solvable subgroup with
$\operatorname{Lie}B=\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ and unipotent
radical $U$. It is maximal connected solvable: every connected solvable closed
subgroup of $G$ containing $B$ equals $B$.

(iii) Repeating the construction with the negative roots produces the closed
connected unipotent subgroup $U^-$ with $\operatorname{Lie}U^-=\mathfrak n^-$
and the closed connected solvable subgroup
$B^-=T\cdot U^-=T\ltimes U^-$ with $\operatorname{Lie}B^-=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^-$.

(iv) The restriction of characters is an isomorphism
$X^*(B)\to X^*(T)$, $\chi\mapsto\chi|_T$.

derivations.claim: Let $V\in\mathcal O_{\chi_\kappa}^{\mathrm{exact}}$. By [F1] it has a finite composition series with factors $L(\lambda)$. Since the central ideal $\ker\chi_\kappa$ annihilates $V$, it annihilates every subquotient; thus each factor has central character $\chi_\kappa$. By [F2], this means $\lambda+\rho$ and $\kappa$ have the same values on all Weyl-invariant polynomials. These invariants separate the finite $W$-orbits: for two disjoint finite orbits, polynomial interpolation separates their point sets, and averaging the separating polynomial over $W$ makes it invariant. Therefore $\lambda+\rho=w\kappa$ for some $w\in W$. Since $\kappa$ is integral, $\lambda$ is integral, and every weight of $L(\lambda)$ differs from $\lambda$ by an element of the root lattice. All weights of $V$ are therefore integral.

For a weight vector $v\in V$, the subspace $U(\mathfrak n^+)v$ is finite-dimensional by [F3] and is stable under $\mathfrak h$, since $[\mathfrak h,\mathfrak n^+]\subseteq\mathfrak n^+$. Its weights are integral by step 1.1. Define the rational $T$-action on each such finite-dimensional subspace by its integral weight characters. Each positive-root operator is nilpotent there because it strictly raises weights in a finite weight set; more generally, a real linear functional positive on all positive roots gives a finite weight filtration strictly raised by every element of $\mathfrak n^+$, so $\pi(X)$ is nilpotent for each $X\in\mathfrak n^+$. The Lie representation of the nilpotent algebra $\mathfrak n^+$ integrates by $u=\exp(X)\mapsto\exp(\pi(X))$: the finite BCH polynomial is respected by the Lie representation, and the exponential coordinates $\mathfrak n^+\to U$ and their multiplication law are those of [F5]. For $t_0\in T$, the weight action satisfies $\rho_T(t_0)\exp(\pi(X))\rho_T(t_0)^{-1}=\exp(\pi(\operatorname{Ad}(t_0)X))$, so [F5] combines the $T$ and $U$ actions into a rational $B=T\ltimes U$-action differentiating to the given $\mathfrak b$-action. Any finite sum of these subspaces is again finite-dimensional and $\mathfrak b$-stable; uniqueness of the exponential $U$-action and the prescribed weight action makes the constructions compatible under inclusions. The subspaces form a directed cover of $V$, so their compatible actions define a rational $B$-action on $V$.

The TDO $\mathcal D_\kappa$ is $G$-equivariant by its action-algebroid construction. The diagonal $B$-action therefore makes $\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa(V)$ strongly $B$-equivariant; it is coherent by [F4]. Conversely, if $M$ is strongly $B$-equivariant and coherent, its global sections inherit a rational $B$-action. The torus action is a direct sum of integral weight spaces, and the unipotent action makes each $U(\mathfrak n^+)$-orbit finite-dimensional. By [F4], $\Gamma M$ is finitely generated over $A_\kappa$, hence over $U(\mathfrak g)$, and its central ideal acts by zero because $A_\kappa$ is the central quotient in [[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. Thus $\Gamma M$ lies in $\mathcal O_{\chi_\kappa}^{\mathrm{exact}}$.

The unit and counit of the equivalence in [F4] are natural and $B$-equivariant, because all functors and maps in their construction commute with the diagonal $B$-action. Their restrictions are still isomorphisms, so the two restricted functors are inverse equivalences.

Assume the complex flag-variety setup, including the Axiom of Choice, of
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. Let $\kappa$ be antidominant, put
$$\Phi_\kappa=\{\beta\in\Phi:\langle\kappa,\beta^\vee\rangle=0\}, \qquad J=\Delta\cap\Phi_\kappa,$$
and assume $J$ is a simple system for the full zero-root subsystem
$\Phi_\kappa$. Choose a reduced expression
$w_J=s_{\alpha_N}\cdots s_{\alpha_1}$ for the longest element of $W_J$.
Set $\mu_0=\rho$, $\mu_j=s_{\alpha_j}\mu_{j-1}$, and
$$H_j=M(-\kappa-\rho+\mu_j),\qquad \mathcal E_j=\mathsf E^B_{\kappa+\rho}(H_j),$$
using the exact twisted associated-bundle functor in
[[lem-pa36-twisted-associated-bundle-and-parabolic-descent]]. The rational
$B$-action has highest-vector weight $\mu_j$. Then there are embeddings
$$H_N\subseteq\cdots\subseteq H_0,\qquad \mathcal E_N\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal E_0 =\mathcal D_\kappa\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(\rho).$$
For each $j$, a coherent module $N_j$ over
$\mathcal D^{\alpha_j}_{\kappa-\rho}$ satisfies
$$\mathcal E_{j-1}/\mathcal E_j\cong \mathcal O_X(\rho)\otimes p_{\alpha_j}^\dagger N_j.$$
Furthermore $\mathcal E_N$ is generated as a $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module by
finitely many global sections: for a finite-dimensional rational irreducible
$G$-module $V$ of highest weight $\rho$ there is a surjection
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\otimes_{\mathbb C}V\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal E_N,$$
with horizontal constant $V$-factor. The sequence of roots depends only on
the chosen reduced expression in $W_J$, not on any later module to which
the chain is applied. When $J$ is empty, $N=0$ and the same assertions hold
with $H_N=H_0$.

Let $\kappa$ be antidominant and let $\alpha$ be a simple root with
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$. Put
$p_\alpha:X=G/B\to X_\alpha=G/P_\alpha$, a Zariski-locally trivial
$\mathbb P^1$-bundle, and let $\rho=\frac12\sum_{\beta\in\Phi^+}\beta$.
Use the partial TDO $\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$ and pullback module
$p_\alpha^\dagger N$ defined in
[[lem-pa36-partial-flag-twist-product]]. For every coherent
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$:

1. $R^q p_{\alpha*}M=0$ for every $q>0$;
2. $p_{\alpha*}M=0$ if and only if there is a coherent
   $\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$-module $N$ with
   $$M\cong\mathcal O_X(\rho)\otimes p_\alpha^\dagger N,$$
   where $N\cong p_{\alpha*}(\mathcal O_X(-\rho)\otimes M)$; this determines $N$ up to canonical isomorphism.

Let $\kappa$ be antidominant, not necessarily regular, and let
$$\Gamma=\Gamma_\kappa:\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa) \longrightarrow A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod},\qquad K=\ker\Gamma.$$
Then $K$ is a Serre subcategory and the induced functors give an equivalence
of abelian categories
$$\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa)/K \simeq A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}.$$
The quotient has representatives precisely among the quasicoherent
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules that are generated by global sections and have no
nonzero quasicoherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-submodule with zero global sections.
No equivalence with the whole $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module category is asserted
without regularity.

Assume the setup of [[def-pa36-global-sections-and-localization]]. If
$\kappa$ is regular antidominant, then
$$\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa:A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod} \rightleftarrows\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa):\Gamma_\kappa$$
are inverse equivalences between all left $A_\kappa$-modules and all
quasi-coherent left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules. The equivalence restricts to
finitely generated $A_\kappa$-modules and coherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules.
It does not assert that $\Gamma$ is faithful for a fixed non-antidominant
representative of a regular central character. Here a coherent
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module means a module locally finitely presented over the
sheaf of rings $\mathcal D_\kappa$; its local noetherianity is part of the
proof below.

Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the
isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying
$$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$
If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$
and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ defines an equivalence between left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules and left $\mathcal D_{\kappa+\eta}$-modules.

derivations.claim: Choose once and for all the reduced expression and its simple-root sequence from [F1]. The explicit proof there constructs the Verma embeddings, their rational simple-parabolic descent, and the central-character projector proving global generation of the final term. Thus this finite chain is an actual local supplier, independent of $M$; it is not an unproved instruction to filter a localization functor. By [F2], each quotient belongs to $\ker p_{\alpha_j*}$.

Suppose the asserted filtration of $M$ exists. Every factor $Q_j$ satisfies $\Gamma(X,Q_j)=\Gamma(X_{\alpha_j},p_{\alpha_j*}Q_j)=0$. Applying exactness [F3] to $0\to M_j\to M_{j-1}\to Q_j\to0$ gives $\Gamma M_{j-1}=\Gamma M_j$. Starting with $M_N=0$ proves $\Gamma M=0$.

Now suppose $\Gamma M=0$. The weight $\kappa-\rho$ is regular antidominant. As proved by the simple-reflection and dual-positive-root calculation in [F1], for every positive root $\beta$, $\langle\rho,\beta^\vee\rangle$ is a positive integer: subtracting it from a nonintegral complex pairing leaves a nonintegral pairing, while subtracting it from a permitted integral pairing, which is nonpositive, gives a strictly negative integer. Thus no positive integral or zero pairing occurs. By the integral twisting equivalence and [F4], $\mathcal O_X(-\rho)\otimes M$ is generated by finitely many global differential sections over $\mathcal D_{\kappa-\rho}$. Tensor back with $\mathcal O_X(\rho)$; the twist bimodule identity gives a surjection $E^n\twoheadrightarrow M$ for some finite $n$, with $E$ as in [F1]. Locally this identity is the equality of line-twisted differential operators from the PBW/twist construction in [F4].

Put $T=\mathcal D_\kappa\Gamma(X,E)\subseteq E$ and $Q=E/T$. The submodule $T$ is the image of the global-section evaluation map and is quasi-coherent; the local filtered-noetherian PBW argument for a TDO makes it coherent as a submodule of the coherent module $E$. Every component $E\to M$ in step 1.3 kills $\Gamma(X,E)$ because $\Gamma M=0$, hence kills $T$, giving a surjection $Q^n\twoheadrightarrow M$. The globally generated submodule $\mathcal E_N\subseteq E$ from [F1] is contained in $T$: each of its global generators is a section of $E$. Therefore the images $Q_j$ of $\mathcal E_j$ in $Q$ give $Q=Q_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq Q_N=0$. Their factors are coherent quotients of $\mathcal E_{j-1}/\mathcal E_j$. Exactness of the corresponding $p_{\alpha_j*}$ in [F2] puts each factor in its kernel.

Take the direct sum of this chain $n$ times and its image under $Q^n\twoheadrightarrow M$. This gives the required finite coherent filtration of $M$ with the same root sequence; every factor is a coherent quotient of a finite sum of factors from step 2.1, and hence has zero corresponding direct image by [F2]. If the sequence is empty, [F1] gives $E=\mathcal E_N$ globally generated, so $T=E$, $Q=0$ and $M=0$, exactly the length-zero filtration. The argument and step 1.2 prove both directions for all the stated complex parameters, with no unproved singular-kernel or derived-localization premise.

Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the
isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying
$$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$
If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$
and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ defines an equivalence between left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules and left $\mathcal D_{\kappa+\eta}$-modules.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from sheaf cohomology. Let $X$ be a
quasi-compact separated scheme ([[def-separated-morphism-schemes]]), let
$U_0,\dots,U_r$ be a finite affine open cover of $X$ and let $\mathcal F$ be a
quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module
([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]). Then every intersection of one or more
members of this cover is affine, and, writing $C^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$
for the ordered Čech cochain complex of the cover in the given order
([[def-cech-cochain-complex-open-cover]]), the canonical comparison map
$$\check H^q(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^q(X,\mathcal F)$$
of the ordered Čech cohomology ([[def-cech-cohomology-open-cover]]) with sheaf
cohomology ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]) is an isomorphism
for every $q\ge0$. The empty scheme is included: its cover may have no
members or any finite number of empty members, and all cochain and cohomology
groups are zero, so the comparison is the unique map $0\to0$. An empty
index set is allowed in this case; $r=0$ gives a one-member cover.

Let $X$ be a scheme ([[def-scheme]]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of
$\mathcal O_X$-modules ([[def-module-on-ringed-space]]). Recall that for a
commutative ring $A$ and an $A$-module $M$ the associated module sheaf
$\widetilde M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the sheaf of
$\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$-modules whose sections on a distinguished
open $D(f)$ are $M_f$
([[def-associated-sheaf-module-affine-scheme]]).

The module $\mathcal F$ is **quasi-coherent** if every point $x\in X$ has an
affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ and an $A$-module
$M$ such that

$$\mathcal F|_U\;\cong\;\widetilde M$$

as sheaves of $\mathcal O_U$-modules. A quasi-coherent sheaf of
$\mathcal O_X$-modules is also called a quasi-coherent module on $X$, and the
full subcategory of $\mathcal O_X$-modules consisting of the quasi-coherent
ones is written $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$; morphisms in
$\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ are all $\mathcal O_X$-module morphisms between its
objects.

Immediate consequences of the definition, used without further comment:

- The condition is invariant under isomorphism: if $\mathcal F\cong\mathcal G$
  as $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, then so is
  $\mathcal G$, because the isomorphism restricts over an affine open.
- The condition is local on $X$: $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent if and only if
  there is an open cover $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ such that each restriction
  $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ is quasi-coherent. Indeed a point of an arbitrary open
  subscheme $U\subseteq X$ has an affine open neighbourhood inside $U$, and an
  affine open subscheme of $X$ contained in $U$ is also an affine open
  subscheme of $U$; conversely, every point of $U_i$ lies in an affine open of
  $X$ inside $U_i$.
- If $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent and $V\subseteq X$ is open, then
  $\mathcal F|_V$ is quasi-coherent, since $\mathcal F|_V$ is again an
  $\mathcal O_V$-module and an affine open $U\subseteq V$ is an affine open of
  $X$.
- On an affine scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ the definition asks at each
  point for an affine open neighbourhood on which $\mathcal F$ is associated to
  a module; it does not ask that $\mathcal F$ itself be associated to a single
  $A$-module. The affine comparison theorem on this page shows that on an
  affine scheme the two conditions coincide.

The terminology follows the standard one: quasi-coherence is the local
affine-module condition, and no finiteness, Noetherian or separatedness
hypothesis is part of it.

derivations.claim: For $\alpha$ the unique positive root, $\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle=c>0$, so $\kappa$ is regular and non-antidominant. By [F1], $M=\mathcal O(-c-1)$ is a left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module, and it is nonzero because it is locally free of rank one.

With $z=y/x$, $w=x/y$ and transition $e_1=z^d e_0$ for $d=-c-1$, the Cech differential has image spanned by nonnegative powers $z^n$ and powers $z^{d-n}$ for $n\ge0$. The first summand gives every exponent $n\ge0$, the second every exponent $n\le -c-1$; the quotient has basis $z^{-c},z^{-c+1},\ldots,z^{-1}$, of size $c$. No exponent belongs to the intersection of those two ranges, so $H^0=0$. Thus $H^1(X,M)\cong\mathbb C^c$ and $\Gamma(X,M)=0$.

Since $M$ is nonzero and quasi-coherent but $\Gamma(M)=0$, the map $0\to M$ proves failure of conservativity. For the standard chart inclusions $j_0,j_1,j_{01}$, put $E=j_{0*}(M|_{U_0})\oplus j_{1*}(M|_{U_1})$ and $F=j_{01*}(M|_{U_0\cap U_1})$. Restriction and difference give a $\mathcal D_\kappa$-linear exact sequence $0\to M\to E\to F\to0$: differential operators act on direct images by restriction, the kernel consists of sections that glue, and on $U_i$ the other direct-image summand maps isomorphically onto $F|_{U_i}$. These sheaves are quasi-coherent by [F4]: on $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[z]$ their distinguished-open sections are the localizations of $\mathbb C[z]e_0$, $(\mathbb C[z]\oplus\mathbb C[z,z^{-1}])e_0$ and $\mathbb C[z,z^{-1}]e_0$, respectively; the same calculation holds with $w,e_1$ on $U_1$. The map $\Gamma(E)\to\Gamma(F)$ is exactly the computed Cech differential with nonzero cokernel. Thus global sections is not exact on quasi-coherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules.
