Write $\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb C)=M_2(\mathbb C)$ for the Lie algebra of
complex $2\times2$ matrices under the commutator bracket
$[A,B]=AB-BA$ ([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]],
[[def-lie-algebra-over-a-field]]). The **special linear Lie algebra**
$\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ is the Lie subalgebra
([[def-lie-subalgebra-ideal-and-center]]) of traceless matrices

$$\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)=\{A\in M_2(\mathbb C):\operatorname{tr}A=0\},$$

which is closed under the bracket because $\operatorname{tr}(AB-BA)=0$. Put

$$e=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad f=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad h=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Direct matrix multiplication gives $he-eh=2e$, $hf-fh=-2f$ and
$ef-fe=h$, that is,

$$[h,e]=2e,\qquad [h,f]=-2f,\qquad [e,f]=h .$$

Since $\{e,f,h\}$ is a basis of the space of traceless matrices, these
relations determine the bracket completely, $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ is
three-dimensional, and $h$ spans a one-dimensional abelian subalgebra.
A Lie algebra over $\mathbb C$ is called a **copy of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$** if it
has a basis $(e,f,h)$ satisfying exactly these three bracket relations.

Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the
isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying
$$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$
If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$
and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ defines an equivalence between left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules and left $\mathcal D_{\kappa+\eta}$-modules.

derivations.claim: The weight of the unique positive root is $2\rho$, so $\rho(h)=1$. With $d=-c-1$, the associated line is $\mathcal O_X((c+1)\rho)=\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(d)$ by [F2]. On $U_0$, the inverse upper-unipotent matrix sends $(1,z)$ to $(1-tz,z)$; therefore its action on a local coefficient $g(z)e_0$ is $(1-tz)^d g(z/(1-tz))e_0$. Differentiating at $t=0$ gives $z^2\partial_z-dz=z^2\partial_z+(c+1)z$ for $e$. The inverse lower unipotent sends $(1,z)$ to $(1,z-t)$, giving $-\partial_z$ for $f$. The inverse diagonal matrix sends $(1,z)$ to $(e^{-t},e^t z)$; the homogeneous frame contributes $e^{-dt}$, so differentiation gives $2z\partial_z-d=2z\partial_z+(c+1)$ for $h$.

On $U_0\cap U_1$, the frames satisfy $e_1=z^d e_0$, so a coefficient $g_1(w)$ on $U_1$ corresponds to $g_0(z)=z^d g_1(1/z)$ on $U_0$. If $Tg_1=z^d g_1(1/z)$, direct differentiation gives $$T^{-1}\partial_zT=d w-w^2\partial_w.$$ Conjugating the three operators from step 1.1 by $T$ and using $d=-(c+1)$ gives, respectively, $-\partial_w$, $w^2\partial_w+(c+1)w$ and $-2w\partial_w-(c+1)$. Thus the two formulas glue. Since they are obtained by differentiating the algebraic $G$-action, their commutators are the brackets in [F1]; direct substitution gives the same relations.
At $c=-1$ one has $d=0$, so the line bundle is the trivial bundle and [F2] gives $\mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X)$, as claimed.

Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the
isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying
$$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$
If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$
and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ defines an equivalence between left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules and left $\mathcal D_{\kappa+\eta}$-modules.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the published group and sheaf
suppliers. Let $G$ be a connected simply connected complex semisimple affine
algebraic group, $B\supseteq T$ a Borel subgroup and maximal torus,
$X=G/B$, $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}G$,
$\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}T$, and $\Phi^+$ the positive roots selected by
$B$. Write $\rho=\frac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$. All schemes are over
$\mathbb C$. For an integral weight $\eta$, $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ denotes the
$G$-equivariant line bundle $G\times^B\mathbb C_\eta$ with fiber character
$\eta$ at $eB$.

The infinitesimal $G$-action gives an anchor
$$a_X:\mathcal L_X:=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathfrak g\longrightarrow T_X,\qquad f\otimes x\longmapsto f x_X.$$
Give $\mathcal L_X$ the action-algebroid bracket
$$[f\otimes x,g\otimes y]=fg\otimes[x,y]+f x_X(g)\otimes y-g y_X(f)\otimes x.$$
Its kernel $\mathfrak b_X=\ker a_X$ is the isotropy Lie-algebra bundle; at
$gB$ its fiber is $\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak b$.

For any $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$, the character $\kappa+\rho$ of
$\mathfrak b$ (zero on $\mathfrak n^+$) transports to an
$\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\chi^X_{\kappa+\rho}:\mathfrak b_X\to\mathcal O_X$.
The transport is independent of the representative $g$ of $gB$, since a
character is invariant under the adjoint action of $B$. The action-algebroid
enveloping sheaf $\mathcal U_X(\mathfrak g)$ is generated by $\mathcal O_X$
and $\mathcal L_X$ with the displayed bracket and
$$[x,f]=x_X(f),\qquad x\in\mathcal L_X,\ f\in\mathcal O_X.$$
Define the sheaf of twisted differential operators
$$\mathcal D_\kappa:=\mathcal U_X(\mathfrak g)/\bigl(\xi-\chi^X_{\kappa+\rho}(\xi):\xi\in\mathfrak b_X\bigr).$$
Its order filtration assigns order zero to $\mathcal O_X$ and order at most
one to the image of $\mathcal L_X$. A TDO means a filtered
$\mathcal O_X$-ring with $F_0=\mathcal O_X$, associated graded
$\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X$, and first-order commutator equal to
the anchor; the well-definedness and PBW properties of $\mathcal D_\kappa$
are proved in [[lem-pa36-flag-tdo-pbw-and-twist]]. A left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module below is required to be quasi-coherent as an
$\mathcal O_X$-module.

For $z\in Z(U(\mathfrak g))$, let $\operatorname{pr}(z)\in U(\mathfrak h)$ be
the Harish–Chandra projection along the chosen triangular decomposition, and
put
$$\chi_\kappa(z)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\kappa-\rho).$$
This is the shifted central character: the Harish–Chandra isomorphism makes it
$W$-invariant in $\kappa$. Define
$$A_\kappa=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\kappa.$$
The regularity convention is **antidominant** when
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\notin\mathbb Z_{>0}$ for each positive
root $\alpha$, and **regular** when
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ne0$ for every root. For complex weights,
$\mathbb Z_{>0}$ means the positive real integers; no order on arbitrary
complex numbers is used.

Let $M$ be a cyclic highest-weight module with highest vector $v$ of weight $\lambda$, and let $z\in Z(U(\mathfrak g))$. Then

$$zv=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\lambda)\,v,$$

so the scalar by which $z$ acts on $M$ is obtained by evaluating the Harish-Chandra projection at $\lambda$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from sheaf cohomology. Let $X$ be a
quasi-compact separated scheme ([[def-separated-morphism-schemes]]), let
$U_0,\dots,U_r$ be a finite affine open cover of $X$ and let $\mathcal F$ be a
quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module
([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]). Then every intersection of one or more
members of this cover is affine, and, writing $C^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$
for the ordered Čech cochain complex of the cover in the given order
([[def-cech-cochain-complex-open-cover]]), the canonical comparison map
$$\check H^q(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^q(X,\mathcal F)$$
of the ordered Čech cohomology ([[def-cech-cohomology-open-cover]]) with sheaf
cohomology ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]) is an isomorphism
for every $q\ge0$. The empty scheme is included: its cover may have no
members or any finite number of empty members, and all cochain and cohomology
groups are zero, so the comparison is the unique map $0\to0$. An empty
index set is allowed in this case; $r=0$ gives a one-member cover.

Let $X$ be a scheme ([[def-scheme]]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of
$\mathcal O_X$-modules ([[def-module-on-ringed-space]]). Recall that for a
commutative ring $A$ and an $A$-module $M$ the associated module sheaf
$\widetilde M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the sheaf of
$\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$-modules whose sections on a distinguished
open $D(f)$ are $M_f$
([[def-associated-sheaf-module-affine-scheme]]).

The module $\mathcal F$ is **quasi-coherent** if every point $x\in X$ has an
affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ and an $A$-module
$M$ such that

$$\mathcal F|_U\;\cong\;\widetilde M$$

as sheaves of $\mathcal O_U$-modules. A quasi-coherent sheaf of
$\mathcal O_X$-modules is also called a quasi-coherent module on $X$, and the
full subcategory of $\mathcal O_X$-modules consisting of the quasi-coherent
ones is written $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$; morphisms in
$\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ are all $\mathcal O_X$-module morphisms between its
objects.

Immediate consequences of the definition, used without further comment:

- The condition is invariant under isomorphism: if $\mathcal F\cong\mathcal G$
  as $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, then so is
  $\mathcal G$, because the isomorphism restricts over an affine open.
- The condition is local on $X$: $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent if and only if
  there is an open cover $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ such that each restriction
  $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ is quasi-coherent. Indeed a point of an arbitrary open
  subscheme $U\subseteq X$ has an affine open neighbourhood inside $U$, and an
  affine open subscheme of $X$ contained in $U$ is also an affine open
  subscheme of $U$; conversely, every point of $U_i$ lies in an affine open of
  $X$ inside $U_i$.
- If $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent and $V\subseteq X$ is open, then
  $\mathcal F|_V$ is quasi-coherent, since $\mathcal F|_V$ is again an
  $\mathcal O_V$-module and an affine open $U\subseteq V$ is an affine open of
  $X$.
- On an affine scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ the definition asks at each
  point for an affine open neighbourhood on which $\mathcal F$ is associated to
  a module; it does not ask that $\mathcal F$ itself be associated to a single
  $A$-module. The affine comparison theorem on this page shows that on an
  affine scheme the two conditions coincide.

The terminology follows the standard one: quasi-coherence is the local
affine-module condition, and no finiteness, Noetherian or separatedness
hypothesis is part of it.

derivations.claim: In type $A_1$, $\rho$ is the fundamental weight and $\mathcal O_X(\rho)=\mathcal O(-1)$. Applying [F1] with $\kappa=0$ and $\eta=\rho$ sends $M=\mathcal O(-1)$ to $M\otimes\mathcal O_X(\rho)=\mathcal O(-2)$ at the new twist $\kappa+\eta=\rho$.

The Harish–Chandra polynomial from [F2] is $p(t)=t+\frac12t^2$ in the $h$-coordinate. At $\kappa=0$, the evaluation point is $\kappa-\rho=-1$, so $p(-1)=-\frac12$. At $\kappa'=\rho$, the evaluation point is $0$, so $p(0)=0$. Thus the central characters differ; also $\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=1$, so the target parameter is non-antidominant.

Put $z=y/x$ on $U_0$ and $w=x/y$ on $U_1$. For $d=-2$, the Cech complex has $C^0=\mathbb C[z]e_0\oplus\mathbb C[w]e_1$ and $C^1=\mathbb C[z,z^{-1}]e_0$, with transition $e_1=z^{-2}e_0$. The image contains powers $z^n$ for $n\ge0$ and $z^{-2-n}$ for $n\ge0$, leaving the single quotient basis $z^{-1}$. Hence $H^0(\mathcal O(-2))=0$ and $\dim H^1(\mathcal O(-2))=1$ by [F3]. The nonzero identity of $M=\mathcal O(-2)$ is killed by global sections, so that functor is not faithful. For the standard chart inclusions $j_0,j_1,j_{01}$, put $E=j_{0*}(M|_{U_0})\oplus j_{1*}(M|_{U_1})$ and $F=j_{01*}(M|_{U_0\cap U_1})$. Restriction and difference give a $\mathcal D_\rho$-linear exact sequence $0\to M\to E\to F\to0$: differential operators act on direct images by restriction, the kernel consists of sections that glue, and on $U_i$ the other direct-image summand maps isomorphically onto $F|_{U_i}$. These sheaves are quasi-coherent by [F5]: on $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[z]$ their distinguished-open sections are the localizations of $\mathbb C[z]e_0$, $(\mathbb C[z]\oplus\mathbb C[z,z^{-1}])e_0$ and $\mathbb C[z,z^{-1}]e_0$, respectively; the same calculation holds with $w,e_1$ on $U_1$. The map $\Gamma(E)\to\Gamma(F)$ is exactly the computed Cech differential with nonzero cokernel. Thus global sections is not exact on quasi-coherent $\mathcal D_\rho$-modules. This computation makes no claim that line-bundle translation preserves global-section faithfulness.

repository basis
$$h=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad e=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad f=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.$$

$$e=-\partial_w,\qquad f=w^2\partial_w+(c+1)w,\qquad h=-2w\partial_w-(c+1).$$

and $h-\lambda(h)$ for $h\in\mathfrak h$; in particular,
$\mathfrak n^+v_\lambda=0$ and $hv_\lambda=\lambda(h)v_\lambda$.

Let $M$ be a cyclic highest-weight module with highest vector $v$ of weight $\lambda$, and let $z\in Z(U(\mathfrak g))$. Then

$$zv=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\lambda)\,v,$$

so the scalar by which $z$ acts on $M$ is obtained by evaluating the Harish-Chandra projection at $\lambda$.

Fix a triangular decomposition $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak n^-\oplus \mathfrak h\oplus \mathfrak n^+$ from [[thm-triangular-decomposition-from-a-chosen-positive-root-system]]. By the PBW basis from [[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]], multiplication gives a vector-space decomposition

$$U(\mathfrak g)=U(\mathfrak h)\oplus \bigl(\mathfrak n^-U(\mathfrak g)+U(\mathfrak g)\mathfrak n^+\bigr).$$

derivations.claim: On the affine chart $U_0$, the module supported at $z=0$ is the Weyl algebra quotient $\mathbb C[z]\langle\partial_z\rangle/ \mathbb C[z]\langle\partial_z\rangle z$. Ordered monomials $\partial_z^n z^m$ show that its global sections have basis $\delta,\partial_z\delta,\partial_z^2\delta,\ldots$; sections vanish off the support point. The relation $z\delta=0$ gives $z\partial_z\delta=-\delta$. Therefore [F1] gives $$e\delta=0,\qquad h\delta=(c+1-2)\delta=(c-1)\delta, \qquad f\delta=-\partial_z\delta.$$

The universal property in [F2] gives a surjection from the Verma module of highest weight $(c-1)\rho$ to $\Gamma(X,\delta_{x_0})$, sending its highest vector to $\delta$. Its PBW basis is $f^n v$ for $n\ge0$, and $f^n\delta=(-1)^n\partial_z^n\delta$ is the basis in step 1.1. The map is therefore an isomorphism.

Since $e\delta=0$ and $h\delta=(c-1)\delta$, the Casimir acts by $$ef\delta+fe\delta+\tfrac12h^2\delta =\bigl((c-1)+\tfrac12(c-1)^2\bigr)\delta =\tfrac12(c^2-1)\delta.$$ In the chosen PBW order, $ef=fe+h$ and the Harish–Chandra projection of $C$ is $h+\tfrac12h^2$. Evaluating it at $\kappa-\rho=(c-1)\rho$ gives the same scalar by [F4]. Thus the module has the exact central character stated.

Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the
isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying
$$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$
If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$
and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ defines an equivalence between left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules and left $\mathcal D_{\kappa+\eta}$-modules.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from sheaf cohomology. Let $X$ be a
quasi-compact separated scheme ([[def-separated-morphism-schemes]]), let
$U_0,\dots,U_r$ be a finite affine open cover of $X$ and let $\mathcal F$ be a
quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module
([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]). Then every intersection of one or more
members of this cover is affine, and, writing $C^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$
for the ordered Čech cochain complex of the cover in the given order
([[def-cech-cochain-complex-open-cover]]), the canonical comparison map
$$\check H^q(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^q(X,\mathcal F)$$
of the ordered Čech cohomology ([[def-cech-cohomology-open-cover]]) with sheaf
cohomology ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]) is an isomorphism
for every $q\ge0$. The empty scheme is included: its cover may have no
members or any finite number of empty members, and all cochain and cohomology
groups are zero, so the comparison is the unique map $0\to0$. An empty
index set is allowed in this case; $r=0$ gives a one-member cover.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Throughout this page,
**$G$ is a connected simply connected complex semisimple affine algebraic
group**: an affine group scheme $G$ of finite type over $\mathbb C$ whose
underlying scheme is connected and smooth, whose Lie algebra
$\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}G$ is a semisimple complex Lie algebra, and
which is simply connected in the sense that every central isogeny
$G'\to G$ of connected affine algebraic groups over $\mathbb C$ with finite
kernel is an isomorphism. These conditions are hypotheses on $G$, fixed once
and for all; the local construction of the root subgroups, of $B$ and of $G/B$
below is where they are used.

**Maximal torus, roots, positive roots.** Fix a maximal torus $T\subseteq G$,
that is, a closed subgroup isomorphic to a product of copies of
$\mathbb G_m$ which is maximal for this property. Its Lie algebra
$\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}T$ is a Cartan subalgebra of $\mathfrak g$ and
$\mathfrak g$ decomposes as
$\mathfrak g=\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi}\mathfrak g_\alpha$
with $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ the root space of the root $\alpha\in\mathfrak h^*$
in the sense of [[def-root-and-root-space-relative-to-a-cartan-subalgebra]].
We write $\Phi=\Phi(G,T)\subseteq\mathfrak h^*$ for this root set, a reduced
crystallographic root system in the real span of $\Phi$, and we fix once and
for all a positive system $\Phi^+$ with simple roots $\Delta$, in the sense of
[[def-positive-system-and-base-of-simple-roots]]. Define the nilpotent Lie
subalgebras
$$\mathfrak n^\pm=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi^\pm}\mathfrak g_\alpha,\qquad \mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+.$$
Here $\mathfrak b$ is the Borel subalgebra of
[[def-positive-and-negative-nilpotent-subalgebras-and-borel-subalgebra]].

**Borel subgroup and unipotent radical.** Reserve $B\subseteq G$ for the
closed connected subgroup with $\operatorname{Lie}B=\mathfrak b$ constructed
in [[lem-semisimple-borel-root-factorization]], and $U\subseteq B$ for its
unipotent radical. That lemma proves $B=T\ltimes U$ and identifies $U$ with
the product of the positive-root subgroups. Reserve $U_\alpha$ for the closed
one-parameter subgroup with $\operatorname{Lie}U_\alpha=\mathfrak g_\alpha$
constructed, with its $T$-equivariance, in
[[lem-semisimple-root-exponential-algebraic-subgroups]]. These symbols name
the later constructions; this definition does not establish their existence.

**Weyl group.** Let $N_G(T)$ be the normalizer subgroup scheme of $T$ in $G$,
and put
$$W=N_G(T)/T .$$
Here the quotient means the fppf quotient sheaf. Its identification with the
constant algebraic group of the abstract Weyl group
$W(\Phi)=\langle s_\alpha:\alpha\in\Phi\rangle$
of [[def-weyl-group-of-a-root-system]] remains a proof obligation for the
later root-representative and Bruhat constructions. Until then $W$ has its
action on $\mathfrak h$ and on $X^*(T)$ by conjugation. The formula does not
identify $W(R)$ with $N_G(T)(R)/T(R)$ for an arbitrary test algebra $R$.

**Flag variety.** Reserve $X=G/B$ for the projective homogeneous
$G$-variety constructed in [[lem-semisimple-projective-orbit-flag-quotients]]
as the orbit of the highest-weight line
$v_B=\wedge^{\dim\mathfrak b}\mathfrak b$ in the Plücker representation
$\wedge^{\dim\mathfrak b}\mathfrak g$. Once constructed, $X(R)$ is the
set of $R$-points of that closed orbit for a $\mathbb C$-algebra $R$. The
represented quotient functor is the fppf sheafification of the presheaf
$R\mapsto G(R)/B(R)$; a given $R$-point lifts to $G(R)$ precisely when its
pulled-back $B$-torsor is trivial. The quotient identification and Zariski
local sections of $G\to X$ are established in
[[lem-semisimple-flag-torsor-zariski-charts]] and
[[thm-semisimple-flag-variety-smooth-projective]].

**Minimal parabolic.** For a simple root $\alpha\in\Delta$, reserve
$P_\alpha$ for the subgroup generated by $B$ and the negative root subgroup
$U_{-\alpha}$. The later lemma
[[lem-semisimple-minimal-parabolic-root-subgroup]] proves that it is closed,
contains $B$ and $U_{-\alpha}$, has
$\operatorname{Lie}P_\alpha=\mathfrak b\oplus\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$,
and satisfies $P_\alpha=B\sqcup Bn_\alpha B$ with $n_\alpha$ a Weyl
representative of $s_\alpha$. That lemma and
[[thm-minimal-parabolic-flag-projection-is-p1-bundle]] prove
$P_\alpha/B\cong\mathbb P^1$ and that $G/B\to G/P_\alpha$ is a Zariski
locally trivial $\mathbb P^1$-bundle.

**Conventions.** All schemes and algebraic groups in this definition and in
every item that depends on it are over $\mathbb C$. The Axiom of Choice is
assumed and is used only through the published Lie-theoretic suppliers of the
root data and through the injective-resolution and sheaf-cohomology supplies
named by the individual items; the finite-type affine-group lemma
[[lem-affine-algebraic-group-faithful-rational-representation]] is choice-free.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be the connected simply connected complex
semisimple affine algebraic group with Borel $B=T\ltimes U$ and Weyl group $W$
of [[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]] and
[[lem-semisimple-borel-root-factorization]], and let $\alpha$ be a simple
root with minimal parabolic $P_\alpha=B\sqcup Bn_\alpha B$, root subgroup
$U_{-\alpha}$ and Weyl subgroup $\{1,s_\alpha\}$ as in
[[lem-semisimple-minimal-parabolic-root-subgroup]]. Let
$\pi_B:G\to X_B$ and $\pi_\alpha:G\to X_\alpha$ be the orbit maps of
[[lem-semisimple-projective-orbit-flag-quotients]]. Then:

(i) the induced map $f:X_B\to X_\alpha$, $g[v_B]\mapsto g[v_\alpha]$, is a
surjective morphism of varieties, well defined because $B\subseteq P_\alpha$,
and its fibre over $g[v_\alpha]$ is canonically the coset space
$P_\alpha/B$, which is $\mathbb P^1$ in the two-chart description
$z\mapsto u_{-\alpha}(z)B$, $t\mapsto u_\alpha(t)n_\alpha B$ with $t=z^{-1}$
of [[lem-semisimple-minimal-parabolic-root-subgroup]];

(ii) $f$ is a Zariski-locally trivial fibre bundle with fibre $\mathbb P^1$: over each single $G$-translate $gV$ of the open torsor chart $V=\sigma_\alpha(U^-_\alpha)\subseteq X_\alpha$ from [[lem-semisimple-flag-torsor-zariski-charts]], it becomes the projection $gV\times\mathbb P^1\to gV$. These translates cover $X_\alpha$ and admit a finite subcover. In the rank-one case $G=P_\alpha$, the base is a point and $f$ is the unique map from $\mathbb P^1$ to that point.

derivations.claim: The twist parameter is $\kappa=0$, so $\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$: it is antidominant and singular under the definitions in [[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. The line bundle $\mathcal O(-1)$ is nonzero and is a $\mathcal D_0$-module by [F1].

Let $z=y/x$ on $U_0$ and $w=x/y$ on $U_1$, with frames related by $e_1=z^{-1}e_0$. The Cech complex has $$C^0=\mathbb C[z]e_0\oplus\mathbb C[w]e_1,\qquad C^1=\mathbb C[z,z^{-1}]e_0,$$ and differential $(f_0,f_1)\mapsto z^{-1}f_1(1/z)-f_0(z)$. A global section would identify a polynomial in nonnegative powers of $z$ with a sum of strictly negative powers, so $H^0=0$. In degree one the image contains all nonnegative powers from $f_0$ and all negative powers from $z^{-1}f_1(1/z)$; these span the Laurent polynomials, so $H^1=0$.

By [F3], $p_\alpha:X\to G/P_\alpha$ is the map to a point. Hence $p_{\alpha*}\mathcal O(-1)=H^0(X,\mathcal O(-1))=0$, while $\mathcal O(-1)\ne0$. The global-sections kernel and the parabolic-pushforward kernel are therefore nonzero, contradicting the refuted assertion. This is the singular Serre-kernel branch, not a counterexample to exactness: the antidominant global-sections functor remains exact by [[thm-pa36-flag-d-affinity]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and a fixed
positive system. Then the maps
$$V\longmapsto\lambda(V),\qquad \lambda\longmapsto L(\lambda)$$
are mutually inverse bijections between the isomorphism classes of
finite-dimensional irreducible representations of $\mathfrak g$ and the
dominant integral weights
([[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]]); here $\lambda(V)$
is the highest weight of $V$
([[def-highest-weight-vector-and-highest-weight-module]]) and $L(\lambda)$ is
the simple quotient of $M_{\mathrm{int}}(\lambda)$.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

Every Verma module $M(\lambda)$, every quotient of it, and every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module belongs to $\mathcal O$.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Let $\{\alpha_i\}_{i\in I}$ be the simple roots of the chosen positive system and write $Q^+=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$ and $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$. Let $W$ be the Weyl group of [[def-root-reflections-and-the-weyl-group-action]] and let $\rho$ be the Weyl vector of [[def-weyl-vector-rho-for-a-chosen-positive-system]]; for $w\in W$ set $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

The **BGG category $\mathcal O$** is the full subcategory of left $U(\mathfrak g)$-modules $M$ satisfying all three conditions: $M$ is finitely generated; $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathfrak h^*}M_\mu$ where $M_\mu=\{v:hv=\mu(h)v\text{ for all }h\in\mathfrak h\}$; and $U(\mathfrak n^+)v$ is finite dimensional for each $v\in M$. Its morphisms are all $\mathfrak g$-linear maps. The zero module is included, generated by the empty set. The enveloping and triangular conventions are those of [[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]] and [[thm-triangular-decomposition-from-a-chosen-positive-root-system]].

Let $M$ be a cyclic highest-weight module with highest vector $v$ of weight $\lambda$, and let $z\in Z(U(\mathfrak g))$. Then

$$zv=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\lambda)\,v,$$

so the scalar by which $z$ acts on $M$ is obtained by evaluating the Harish-Chandra projection at $\lambda$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra, let $\mathfrak h$ be any Cartan subalgebra in the
nilpotent self-normalizing sense, and fix a positive root system with Weyl
group $W$ and half-sum $\rho$ of its positive roots. The shifted Harish-Chandra map

$$ \operatorname{HC}_\rho\colon Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to S(\mathfrak h)^W, \qquad \operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)(\lambda)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\lambda-\rho), $$

is an algebra isomorphism.

Let $\kappa$ be integral, regular and antidominant. Define the **exact
central-character subcategory**
$$\mathcal O_{\chi_\kappa}^{\mathrm{exact}} =\{V\in\mathcal O:(\ker\chi_\kappa)V=0\}.$$
A **strongly $B$-equivariant coherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module** means a
coherent left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module with a rational $B$-linearization
whose differential is the action-algebroid action and whose action is
compatible with the $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module structure. Then
$\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa$ and $\Gamma_\kappa$ restrict to inverse
equivalences between $\mathcal O_{\chi_\kappa}^{\mathrm{exact}}$ and these
strongly $B$-equivariant coherent modules.

The exact subcategory is distinct from the generalized-character block, where
each vector is killed by some power of $\ker\chi_\kappa$; the theorem does not
identify the whole generalized block with $B$-equivariant coherent modules.

derivations.claim: By [F1], $V(n\rho)$ is finite-dimensional and irreducible. Its Cartan action is diagonalizable, so [F2] places it in $\mathcal O$. Schur's lemma makes every central element act by a scalar; evaluating on a highest vector and using [F3], its central character is $\chi_{n\rho+\rho}= \chi_{(n+1)\rho}$.

In type $A_1$, $s\rho=-\rho$, so $s((n+1)\rho)=-(n+1)\rho=\kappa$. W-invariance in [F3] gives $\chi_\kappa=\chi_{(n+1)\rho}$. The pairing $\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle=-(n+1)$ is nonzero and nonpositive, so $\kappa$ is regular antidominant.

The central ideal $\ker\chi_\kappa$ annihilates $V(n\rho)$ exactly, not merely by a power, because its central character is $\chi_\kappa$ by step 2.1. Thus it belongs to the exact subcategory in [F4], and that corollary gives the asserted coherent strongly B-equivariant localization. The generalized-character condition permits nilpotent action of the central ideal and is not used in this example.

Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the
isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying
$$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$
If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$
and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ defines an equivalence between left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules and left $\mathcal D_{\kappa+\eta}$-modules.

Assume the flag-variety setup of
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. If $\kappa$ is antidominant, then every
quasi-coherent left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$ satisfies
$$H^i(X,M)=0\qquad(i>0).$$
Moreover, $\Gamma(X,-)$ is exact on the category of quasi-coherent left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules.
If $\kappa$ is also regular, then $\Gamma(X,M)=0$ implies $M=0$. The
antidominance and regularity conditions are independent hypotheses; regularity
alone does not imply the vanishing assertion.

Assume the setup of [[def-pa36-global-sections-and-localization]]. If
$\kappa$ is regular antidominant, then
$$\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa:A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod} \rightleftarrows\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa):\Gamma_\kappa$$
are inverse equivalences between all left $A_\kappa$-modules and all
quasi-coherent left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules. The equivalence restricts to
finitely generated $A_\kappa$-modules and coherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules.
It does not assert that $\Gamma$ is faithful for a fixed non-antidominant
representative of a regular central character. Here a coherent
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module means a module locally finitely presented over the
sheaf of rings $\mathcal D_\kappa$; its local noetherianity is part of the
proof below.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from sheaf cohomology.

For $d\in\mathbb Z$, let $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(d)$ have standard
frames $e_0,e_1$ on $U_0=\{x\ne0\}$ and $U_1=\{y\ne0\}$ with
$e_1=z^d e_0$ on the overlap, where $z=y/x$ and $w=1/z$. Then
$$\dim H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(d))=\max(d+1,0),\qquad \dim H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(d))=\max(-d-1,0),$$
and $H^q=0$ for $q\ge2$. For $d\ge0$, restrictions to $U_0$ of global
sections on $\mathbb P^1$, written in the frame $e_0$, are precisely
the polynomials of degree at most $d$; for $d\le-2$, $H^1$ has Laurent
basis $z^{d+1},z^{d+2},\ldots,z^{-1}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from sheaf cohomology and from the
derived direct-image construction. Let $f:X\to S$ be an affine morphism of
schemes ([[def-affine-morphism-schemes]]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a
quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module
([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]). Then, with $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ the
higher direct images ([[def-higher-direct-image-sheaf]]),
$$R^qf_*\mathcal F=0$$
for every $q>0$. The empty source and target, the zero module, the identity
morphism and the case where $S$ is affine are included; $q=0$ is not asserted
to vanish, since $R^0f_*\mathcal F=f_*\mathcal F$ need not be zero.

Let $\alpha$ be a simple root, $P_\alpha$ its minimal parabolic,
$Y=G/P_\alpha$, and $p_\alpha:X=G/B\to Y$. Let
$\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ satisfy $\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$.
The restriction of $\kappa$ to $\mathfrak p_\alpha$ that is zero on root
spaces is a Lie algebra character. Define the partial-flag TDO
$\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$ on $Y$ as the action-algebroid quotient
whose isotropy character is this restriction of $\kappa$; the subscript
$\kappa-\rho$ uses the convention that a TDO parameter $\nu$ has isotropy
character $\nu+\rho$. For a quasicoherent left
$\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$-module $N$, define $p_\alpha^\dagger N$
on a Zariski product chart $p_\alpha^{-1}(U)\cong U\times\mathbb P^1$ to be
the ordinary inverse-image module $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}\boxtimes N|_U$: relative vector fields differentiate the first factor, and base operators act on the second. Its underlying sheaf is $\mathcal O_X\otimes_{p_\alpha^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}p_\alpha^{-1}N$; the differential transition maps are induced by the chain rule under changes of the $P_\alpha$-torsor section. Then
these local modules glue to a quasicoherent left
$\mathcal D_{\kappa-\rho}$-module, and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\rho)$
turns it into a left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module. The restriction of
$\mathcal O_X(\rho)$ to each $p_\alpha$-fiber is
$\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$.

For a torsor section $s:U\to G$, the product chart used below is the
commutative square whose top arrow is $\Phi_s(u,qB)=s(u)qB$:

```tikzcd
U\times P_\alpha/B \arrow[r,"\Phi_s"] \arrow[d,"\mathrm{pr}_1"'] & p_\alpha^{-1}(U) \arrow[d,"p_\alpha"] \\
U \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}_U"'] & U
```

The left vertical map is projection, and the bottom map is identity. The
torsor section makes $\Phi_s$ an isomorphism; the equality
$p_\alpha\circ\Phi_s=\mathrm{pr}_1$ verifies commutativity. The diagram
records the local chart only; the PBW and gluing arguments below prove the
TDO identifications.

derivations.claim: Morita untwisting identifies $E$ with $L\otimes D$. Its evaluation map $\epsilon:E\to L$ sends $\ell\otimes P$ to $\ell P(1)$. In an affine coordinate $x$, the unique normal form $P=\sum_{j\ge0}a_j\partial_x^j$ shows that $K=\ker\epsilon$ is locally $L\otimes D\partial_x$. Its order-one part is canonically $L\otimes T_Z$: a vector field intrinsically annihilates $1$, so this identification does not choose a connection or coordinate. PBW shows $K=D_0K_{\le1}$. By [F3] the two global sections of $K_{\le1}=\mathcal O_Z(1)$ generate $K$. Conversely every global section of $E$ maps to zero because $\Gamma L=0$. Thus $D_0\Gamma E=K$, proving the universal quotient.

Let $q:Z\times U\to Z$ be the other projection. It is affine, so $q_*Q$ is quasi-coherent, carries the relative $D_0$-action, and has no positive higher direct images by [F4]. Leray and singular vanishing [F2] give $H^i(Z\times U,Q)=0$ for $i>0$. Apply the same argument over every affine open subset of $U$; the sheafification of these cohomology groups is $R^i r_*Q$, proving its vanishing. In particular $r_*$ is exact on quasi-coherent product differential modules.

Put $T=L^{-1}\otimes Q$. By the regular equivalence in [F2], $T$ is generated over $D$ by its global sections, so $E^{(I)}\twoheadrightarrow Q$ for some set $I$. Since $\Gamma Q=0$, each summand kills $\Gamma E$ and hence $D_0\Gamma E$. Step 1.1 gives $L^{(I)}\twoheadrightarrow Q$, or $\mathcal O_Z^{(I)}\twoheadrightarrow T$. The kernel $H$ is a quasi-coherent $D$-module. Exactness of $\Gamma$ embeds $\Gamma H$ into $\mathbb C^{(I)}$; its $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action is trivial. The natural map $\mathcal O_Z\otimes_{\mathbb C}\Gamma H\to H$ sends a constant horizontal section to that same section, and is $D$-linear because $H\subseteq\mathcal O_Z^{(I)}$. Its map on global sections is the identity of $\Gamma H$. Exactness and regular conservativity in [F2] kill its kernel and cokernel, so it is an isomorphism. Thus $H=\mathcal O_Z\otimes\Gamma H$ and $T=\mathcal O_Z\otimes V$, with $V=\Gamma T$. Untwisting gives the claimed canonical evaluation isomorphism and trivial action. The converse follows from $\Gamma L=0$.

For any central base ring $R$, push a module on $Z_R=Z\times\operatorname{Spec}R$ along the affine map to $Z$ and apply step 2.1. Multiplication by $R$ commutes with all vertical operators, so its natural evaluation is $R$-linear and reconstructs the sheaf as $L_R\otimes_R N$. Conversely this form has zero direct image by the Čech complex for $L$ tensored over $\mathbb C$ with $N$. Tensoring this form over $R$ with $R'$ proves the asserted scalar-extension compatibility without assuming flatness. If $R$ is noetherian, finite relative differential generators involve finitely many coefficients in $N$; these coefficients generate $N$ since vertical operators create no new coefficients. Conversely finitely generated $N$ gives a finite relative differential generating set, and PBW over the noetherian ring $R$ makes the relative differential ring left noetherian, proving coherence.

Suppose $r_*Q=0$. Then $\Gamma(Z,q_*Q)=\Gamma(Z\times U,Q)=0$. Step 2.1 applied to $q_*Q$ yields its canonical form $L\otimes V$. Multiplication by $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ and every operator in $\Gamma(U,A)$ commute with the relative $D_0$ action, so naturality of step 2.1 makes $V$ a module over that base differential ring. Affine quasi-coherent sheafification identifies its sheaf with $N=r_*(L^{-1}\otimes Q)$ and the obtained isomorphism with $Q=L\boxtimes N$. No tensor product is taken over a noncommutative ring: the exterior product is over $\mathbb C$ with the two commuting actions. Conversely $r_*(L\boxtimes N)=0$ follows by the two-affine-open Čech calculation for $L$ tensored over $\mathbb C$ with $N$.

The $A$-module $N$ of step 3.2 is coherent. On each of the two affine fiber charts choose finitely many product-differential generators of $Q$. This is possible for a coherent differential module on an affine smooth chart: its quasi-coherent underlying module is determined by sections; local finite generators on a finite principal-open cover become global generators after clearing denominators, and differential operators localize by the Leibniz rule. Trivialize $L$ there and express each chosen generator as a finite sum of polynomials in the fiber coordinate times sections of $N$. Let $N_0$ be the base differential submodule generated by the finitely many coefficients from both charts. Product differential operators preserve $L\boxtimes N_0$, so the chosen generators imply $L\boxtimes N_0=L\boxtimes N$. Evaluation at any fiber point gives $N_0=N$, proving finite generation. A TDO on a smooth affine chart is left noetherian: PBW gives the noetherian graded algebra $\operatorname{Sym}T_U$; lift finitely many graded generators and induct on order to generate any left ideal. Thus finite generation implies coherence.

Finally the map $p^\dagger p_*(L^{-1}\otimes Q)\to L^{-1}\otimes Q$ is the intrinsic differential evaluation map. On each product chart it is the isomorphism of step 3.2. A change of torsor section acts on the fiber coordinate by its transition, and the chain rule intertwines relative differentiation; the base differential action transforms by the given TDO cocycle. Evaluation therefore agrees on overlaps and glues. Moreover $p_*p^\dagger N=N$, since $p_*\mathcal O=\mathcal O$ on a $\mathbb P^1$-bundle, so $N$ is unique up to its canonical isomorphism. The argument uses choice only for the permitted bases and generating sets in [F2] and the inherited suppliers.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be the connected simply connected complex
semisimple affine algebraic group with maximal torus $T$, root system $\Phi$,
positive system $\Phi^+$, Borel subgroup $B=T\ltimes U$, opposite unipotent
subgroup $U^-$ and Weyl group $W=N_G(T)/T$ of
[[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]] and
[[lem-semisimple-borel-root-factorization]], fix a simple root
$\alpha\in\Delta$ with minimal parabolic $P_\alpha$ as in
[[lem-semisimple-minimal-parabolic-root-subgroup]], put
$U^-_\alpha=\prod_{\beta\in\Phi^+,\ \beta\neq\alpha}U_{-\beta}$, and let
$X_B=G/B\subseteq\mathbb P(W_B)$ and
$X_\alpha=G/P_\alpha\subseteq\mathbb P(W_\alpha)$ be the closed orbits with
orbit maps $\pi_B:G\to X_B$, $\pi_\alpha:G\to X_\alpha$ of
[[lem-semisimple-projective-orbit-flag-quotients]]. Write
$\Omega=U^-B$ for the open big cell. Then:

(i) the orbit map restricted to $\Omega$ factors through the projection
$\Omega\to\Omega/B\cong U^-$ as an injective morphism
$\sigma_B:U^-\to X_B$ with
$\pi_B^{-1}\bigl(\sigma_B(U^-)\bigr)=\Omega$ and
$\sigma_B(U^-)\times B\cong\Omega$ exhibiting $\pi_B$ as the trivial
$B$-torsor over the chart $\sigma_B(U^-)$; the same holds for $\pi_\alpha$ with
the morphism $\sigma_\alpha:U^-_\alpha\to X_\alpha$, $\sigma_\alpha(u)=u[v_\alpha]$,
the subgroup $P_\alpha$ in place of $B$, and the open subset
$U^-_\alpha P_\alpha\subseteq G$ in place of $\Omega$;

(ii) each chart in (i) is a Zariski-open subscheme of its orbit, and all its single $G$-translates cover that orbit. Every translate has the transported product trivialization. Since the projective orbits are quasi-compact, finite subfamilies of these open translates also cover them;

(iii) consequently $\pi_B$ and $\pi_\alpha$ represent Zariski-locally trivial right $B$- and $P_\alpha$-torsors. Their fppf sheaf quotients are $X_B$ and $X_\alpha$, and each associated bundle, including $G\times^B\mathbb C_{-\lambda}$, is Zariski locally trivial on the translated charts.

Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the
isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying
$$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$
If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$
and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ defines an equivalence between left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules and left $\mathcal D_{\kappa+\eta}$-modules.

For $\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*$, the **Verma module** is the induced
$\mathfrak g$-module

$$M(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\mathbb C_\lambda,$$

where $U(\mathfrak g)$ is the quotient algebra of
[[def-universal-enveloping-algebra-as-a-tensor-quotient]] and
$\mathbb C_\lambda$ is [[def-one-dimensional-borel-module-of-weight-lambda]].
Write $v_\lambda:=1\otimes c_\lambda$.  Thus $M(\lambda)$ is the quotient of
$U(\mathfrak g)$ by the left ideal generated by $x$ for $x\in\mathfrak n^+$
and $h-\lambda(h)$ for $h\in\mathfrak h$; in particular,
$\mathfrak n^+v_\lambda=0$ and $hv_\lambda=\lambda(h)v_\lambda$.

Let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be an ordered basis of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Then the monomials

$$x_1^{a_1}x_2^{a_2}\cdots x_r^{a_r} \qquad (a_i\in \mathbb N_0)$$

form a basis of $U(\mathfrak g)$. In particular, multiplication identifies $\operatorname{gr}U(\mathfrak g)$ with the symmetric algebra $S(\mathfrak g)$ on the symbols of the $x_i$.

Let $\alpha$ be a simple root, $P_\alpha$ its minimal parabolic,
$Y=G/P_\alpha$, and $p_\alpha:X=G/B\to Y$. Let
$\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ satisfy $\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$.
The restriction of $\kappa$ to $\mathfrak p_\alpha$ that is zero on root
spaces is a Lie algebra character. Define the partial-flag TDO
$\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$ on $Y$ as the action-algebroid quotient
whose isotropy character is this restriction of $\kappa$; the subscript
$\kappa-\rho$ uses the convention that a TDO parameter $\nu$ has isotropy
character $\nu+\rho$. For a quasicoherent left
$\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$-module $N$, define $p_\alpha^\dagger N$
on a Zariski product chart $p_\alpha^{-1}(U)\cong U\times\mathbb P^1$ to be
the ordinary inverse-image module $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}\boxtimes N|_U$: relative vector fields differentiate the first factor, and base operators act on the second. Its underlying sheaf is $\mathcal O_X\otimes_{p_\alpha^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}p_\alpha^{-1}N$; the differential transition maps are induced by the chain rule under changes of the $P_\alpha$-torsor section. Then
these local modules glue to a quasicoherent left
$\mathcal D_{\kappa-\rho}$-module, and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\rho)$
turns it into a left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module. The restriction of
$\mathcal O_X(\rho)$ to each $p_\alpha$-fiber is
$\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$.

For a torsor section $s:U\to G$, the product chart used below is the
commutative square whose top arrow is $\Phi_s(u,qB)=s(u)qB$:

```tikzcd
U\times P_\alpha/B \arrow[r,"\Phi_s"] \arrow[d,"\mathrm{pr}_1"'] & p_\alpha^{-1}(U) \arrow[d,"p_\alpha"] \\
U \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}_U"'] & U
```

The left vertical map is projection, and the bottom map is identity. The
torsor section makes $\Phi_s$ an isomorphism; the equality
$p_\alpha\circ\Phi_s=\mathrm{pr}_1$ verifies commutativity. The diagram
records the local chart only; the PBW and gluing arguments below prove the
TDO identifications.

derivations.claim: The relation $[gs,h]=[g,r(s)h]$ defines the associated sheaf by [F1]; rationality means every vector belongs to a finite-dimensional rational $S$-submodule, so the construction is the filtered union of the usual finite-rank associated bundles. On a torsor section it is precisely $\mathcal O_Y\otimes H$. A short exact sequence of twisted modules therefore becomes a short exact sequence of sheaves, since tensoring over $\mathbb C$ is exact. Equivariant morphisms give the same local maps on all charts.

Let $\beta(A)$ be the infinitesimal $G$-action on the associated sheaf. Define an $\mathcal O_Y$-linear action by $$\gamma(A)[g,h]=[g,\pi(\operatorname{Ad}(g^{-1})A)h].$$ The covariance hypothesis makes this independent of replacing $g$ by $gs$. Differentiating covariance gives $[\beta(A),\gamma(A')]=\gamma([A,A'])$; the representation property gives $[\gamma(A),\gamma(A')]=\gamma([A,A'])$. Consequently $a(A)=\beta(A)-\gamma(A)$ satisfies $$[a(A),f]=A_Y(f),\qquad [a(A),a(A')]=a([A,A']).$$ At the base point, an isotropy element $x\in\mathfrak s$ acts by $dr(x)-\pi(x)=\tau(x)$; transport gives the same isotropy relation at every point. Thus $a$ factors through $\mathcal A^S_\tau$. The displayed identities also show that maps in step 1.1 are differential-module maps, proving exactness of the differential functor.

The associated-bundle map for a finite $G$-module is $$[g,h\otimes v]\longmapsto[g,h]\otimes gv.$$ It respects the $S$ relation; its inverse sends $[g,h]\otimes w$ to $[g,h\otimes g^{-1}w]$. Under this map $\beta$ becomes $\beta_H\otimes1+1\otimes dV$, because the $G$-equivariant structure on the trivial bundle has the diagonal $G$-action. Likewise $\gamma$ becomes $\gamma_H\otimes1+1\otimes dV$: the identity $g\,dV(\operatorname{Ad}(g^{-1})A)\,g^{-1}=dV(A)$ gives its second summand. Subtraction cancels these finite-representation terms exactly. Thus $a=a_H\otimes1$, with the Leibniz rule on function coefficients, and constant vectors of $V$ are horizontal. This proves the asserted identity as a differential-module identity, not merely as an equivariant bundle identity.

More generally fix an integral $B$-weight $\eta$ and put $\tau=\kappa+\rho$. On $M(-\tau+\eta)$ define the rational $B$-action by conjugating the $U(\mathfrak g)$ factor and letting the highest vector have weight $\eta$. The infinitesimal action is $\pi+\tau$: commuting $x\in\mathfrak b$ past the enveloping factor leaves the scalar $(-\tau+\eta)(x)$ on the highest vector, whereas the rational action leaves $\eta(x)$. Its rationality follows from the finite-dimensional adjoint filtration of $U(\mathfrak g)$ and the rational character $\eta$. The highest line gives a line subbundle $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ of the associated sheaf. Apply the differential action to obtain $\mathcal D_\kappa\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(\eta) \to\mathsf E^B_\tau(M(-\tau+\eta))$. Locally on a torsor section, filter both sides by the degree of the negative-root PBW monomials. On the right, $\gamma$ supplies those monomials with sign $-1$ and $\beta$ preserves the associated filtration; hence the leading map sends a degree-$d$ tangent monomial to $(-1)^d$ times the corresponding Verma monomial. By [F2]–[F3] this is an isomorphism of symmetric tangent modules. Induction on degree therefore proves the filtered map is an isomorphism. The cases $\eta=0,\rho$ are the claimed formulas.

For twisted $(\mathfrak g,P_\alpha)$-module $H$ of twist $\kappa$, the character $\kappa$ is defined on $\mathfrak p_\alpha$ because its $\alpha$-coroot pairing is zero. The construction of steps 1.1 and 2.1 on $Y=G/P_\alpha$ gives $N$ over $\mathcal A^{P_\alpha}_\kappa =\mathcal D^\alpha_{\kappa-\rho}$. Restriction from $P_\alpha$ to $B$ identifies associated underlying sheaves $G\times^B H=p_\alpha^*(G\times^{P_\alpha}H)$. In a product chart its underlying module is $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}\boxtimes N$. For a vertical vector field, its $\beta$ and fiberwise $\gamma$ terms on the transported $H$ cancel, leaving only differentiation of the relative function coefficient. For base fields the same formula is the original $\beta-\gamma$ action on $N$. These are precisely the ordinary inverse image action in [F4]. They also prove agreement on overlaps, since both sides use the same $P_\alpha$ transition and chain rule. Thus $\mathsf E^B_\kappa(H)=p_\alpha^\dagger N$.

Multiplying the restricted rational $B$-action by the integral character $\rho$ adds $\rho$ to its differential while leaving $\pi$ unchanged. The associated bundle is therefore tensored by $\mathcal O_X(\rho)$. By [F2] its differential twist becomes $\kappa+\rho$, so its TDO is $\mathcal D_\kappa$. Combine this with step 3.3 to obtain the displayed parabolic-descent identity. Choices of bases and of local torsor sections use only the inherited Axiom of Choice; all resulting constructions and isomorphisms are canonical.

citations.quote: Every $W$-orbit in $E$ has exactly one point in $\overline{\mathcal C}$. For $\eta\in\overline{\mathcal C}$, its stabilizer is generated by those simple reflections $s_i$ with $(\eta,\alpha_i)=0$. The group acts simply transitively on open chambers. There is a unique longest element $w_0$, characterized by $w_0\Phi^+=\Phi^-$; it has length $|\Phi^+|$ and satisfies $w_0^2=1$. In particular every weight orbit has a unique dominant weight. These assertions include rank zero and singular wall points, without AC.

For the preceding finite reduced crystallographic root system, regular vectors $t$ exist, $W$ is finite, and the simple positive roots are a basis of $E$. Every root has integral coordinates in this basis of one sign. Each $s_i$ permutes $\Phi^+\setminus\{\alpha_i\}$ and sends $\alpha_i$ to $-\alpha_i$. The simple reflections generate $W$, and every root is the image of a simple root under their group. The simple coroots similarly form an integral basis of the coroot group, and $P$ is the lattice generated by their dual basis; $W$ preserves $Q,Q^\vee,P$. All assertions are choice-free, including rank zero.

For the simple reflections of a finite reduced crystallographic root system, word length equals inversion length: $\ell(w)=|\operatorname{Inv}(w)|$. If a root reflection $t$ satisfies $\ell(tw)<\ell(w)$, every reduced word for $w$ loses exactly one letter to give $tw$. Every nonreduced word admits deletion of two letters without changing its group element.

More precisely, for $\beta\in\Phi^+$, $\ell(s_\beta w)<\ell(w)$ if and only if $w^{-1}\beta<0$. In this case one letter can be deleted from any word for $w$ to give $s_\beta w$, although the resulting word need not be reduced. Also $\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)\pm1$, with the minus sign exactly when $w\alpha_i<0$. These are assertions for the geometric reflection group, without an assumed Coxeter presentation or exchange axiom.

Let $E$ be the real span of a finite reduced crystallographic root system
$\Phi$, with chosen positive roots $\Phi^+$, simple roots
$\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r\}$, Weyl group $W$ and root lattice
$Q=\sum_i\mathbb Z\alpha_i$. Extend the pairing complex linearly to
$E_\mathbb C$. For $\kappa\in E_\mathbb C$, call $\kappa$ antidominant if
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\notin\mathbb Z_{>0}$ for every
$\alpha\in\Phi^+$, and regular if
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ne0$ for every root. Then
$$\kappa-w\kappa\notin Q_+\setminus\{0\}\qquad(w\in W)$$
for antidominant $\kappa$, and
$$\kappa-w\kappa\notin Q_+\qquad(w\ne1)$$
when $\kappa$ is also regular. Here
$Q_+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\lambda\in X^*(T)$.
If $\lambda$ is not dominant integral then $H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$. If
$\lambda$ is dominant integral then
$H^0(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)\cong L(\lambda)^*$ as $\mathfrak g$-modules, and
$H^i(X,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0$ for every $i>0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and a fixed
positive system with Weyl group $W$ and fundamental chamber $C$
([[def-open-and-closed-weyl-chambers]],
[[thm-the-weyl-group-acts-simply-transitively-on-weyl-chambers]]),
let $\lambda$ be dominant integral, and let $V(\lambda)$ be the
finite-dimensional irreducible module of highest weight $\lambda$. Then for
every $w\in W$ the weight $w(\lambda)$ occurs in $V(\lambda)$ with multiplicity
one,
$$\dim V(\lambda)_{w(\lambda)}=1 ,$$
and $w(\lambda)$ is extremal in the chamber $w(C)$, in the following sense:
every weight $\mu$ of $V(\lambda)$ satisfies $w^{-1}(\mu)\le\lambda$ in the root
order, equivalently $w(\lambda)-\mu$ is a nonnegative integral combination of
the positive roots of the positive system defined by the chamber $w(C)$.

For $\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*$, the **Verma module** is the induced
$\mathfrak g$-module

$$M(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\mathbb C_\lambda,$$

where $U(\mathfrak g)$ is the quotient algebra of
[[def-universal-enveloping-algebra-as-a-tensor-quotient]] and
$\mathbb C_\lambda$ is [[def-one-dimensional-borel-module-of-weight-lambda]].
Write $v_\lambda:=1\otimes c_\lambda$.  Thus $M(\lambda)$ is the quotient of
$U(\mathfrak g)$ by the left ideal generated by $x$ for $x\in\mathfrak n^+$
and $h-\lambda(h)$ for $h\in\mathfrak h$; in particular,
$\mathfrak n^+v_\lambda=0$ and $hv_\lambda=\lambda(h)v_\lambda$.

Let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be an ordered basis of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Then the monomials

$$x_1^{a_1}x_2^{a_2}\cdots x_r^{a_r} \qquad (a_i\in \mathbb N_0)$$

form a basis of $U(\mathfrak g)$. In particular, multiplication identifies $\operatorname{gr}U(\mathfrak g)$ with the symmetric algebra $S(\mathfrak g)$ on the symbols of the $x_i$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra, let $\mathfrak h$ be any Cartan subalgebra in the
nilpotent self-normalizing sense, and fix a positive root system with Weyl
group $W$ and half-sum $\rho$ of its positive roots. The shifted Harish-Chandra map

$$ \operatorname{HC}_\rho\colon Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to S(\mathfrak h)^W, \qquad \operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)(\lambda)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\lambda-\rho), $$

is an algebra isomorphism.

Assume the complex simply connected semisimple setup, including the Axiom of
Choice, of [[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. Let $S$ be $B$ or a minimal
parabolic $P_\alpha$, put $Y=G/S$, and let $\tau$ be an
$\operatorname{Ad}(S)$-invariant character of $\mathfrak s$. A
**twisted $(\mathfrak g,S)$-module of twist $\tau$** means a vector space
$H$ with a Lie representation $\pi:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}H$ and
a rational $S$-representation $r$, such that
$$d r(x)=\pi(x)+\tau(x)\operatorname{id}_H\quad(x\in\mathfrak s),\qquad r(s)\pi(A)r(s)^{-1}=\pi(\operatorname{Ad}(s)A).$$
The weight $\tau$ can be complex; no rational character $s\mapsto s^\tau$
is presumed. Define $\mathcal A^S_\tau$ by the action-algebroid quotient on
$Y$ with isotropy character $\tau$, and define
$$\mathsf E^S_\tau(H)=G\times^S(H,r).$$
For infinite-dimensional rational modules, this is the associated
quasi-coherent sheaf, locally $\mathcal O_Y\otimes_{\mathbb C}H$.
Then $\mathsf E^S_\tau$ is an exact functor to quasi-coherent
$\mathcal A^S_\tau$-modules. For $S=B$,
$\mathcal A^B_{\kappa+\rho}=\mathcal D_\kappa$.

If $V$ is a finite-dimensional rational $G$-module, use the diagonal Lie
and $S$ actions on $H\otimes V$. Then
$$\mathsf E^S_\tau(H\otimes V)\cong \mathsf E^S_\tau(H)\otimes_{\mathbb C}V,$$
where the differential action on the right acts only on the first factor:
constant vectors in $V$ are horizontal. In particular, with
$M(\lambda)=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\mathbb C_\lambda$,
$$\mathsf E^B_{\kappa+\rho}(M(-\kappa-\rho))\cong\mathcal D_\kappa, \qquad \mathsf E^B_{\kappa+\rho}(M(-\kappa))\cong \mathcal D_\kappa\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(\rho).$$
In these formulas the rational $B$-action is the adjoint action on the
induced module with its highest vector of twisted weight $0$ or $\rho$,
respectively; the tensor product on the last right-hand side uses the right
$\mathcal O_X$-action on $\mathcal D_\kappa$.

Finally suppose $\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$ and $H$ is twisted
$(\mathfrak g,P_\alpha)$ of twist $\kappa$. Let
$N=\mathsf E^{P_\alpha}_\kappa(H)$, a module over the partial TDO
$\mathcal D^\alpha_{\kappa-\rho}$ of
[[lem-pa36-partial-flag-twist-product]]. Restrict its rational action to
$B$ and tensor that rational action by the integral character $\rho$;
with unchanged $\pi$ this makes $H$ twisted of twist $\kappa+\rho$.
For this latter structure,
$$\mathsf E^B_{\kappa+\rho}(H)\cong \mathcal O_X(\rho)\otimes p_\alpha^\dagger N.$$
Here $p_\alpha^\dagger$ is ordinary differential inverse image, with local
underlying sheaf $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}\boxtimes N$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be the connected simply connected complex
semisimple affine algebraic group with maximal torus $T$, root system $\Phi$ and
positive system $\Phi^+$ fixed in
[[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]], and for
$\alpha\in\Phi^+$ let $u_\alpha:\mathbb G_a\to U_\alpha$ be the root subgroup
constructed in [[lem-semisimple-root-exponential-algebraic-subgroups]]. Fix a
total order $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_m$ of $\Phi^+$ compatible with heights, that
is $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha_i)\le\operatorname{ht}(\alpha_j)$ whenever $i<j$.

Then the following hold.

(i) The product map
$$\prod_{i=1}^mU_{\alpha_i}\longrightarrow G,\qquad (g_1,\dots,g_m)\longmapsto g_1g_2\cdots g_m,$$
is an isomorphism of varieties onto a closed connected unipotent subgroup
$U\subseteq G$ with $\operatorname{Lie}U=\mathfrak n^+$ and $\dim U=|\Phi^+|$;
explicitly $(z_1,\dots,z_m)\mapsto u_{\alpha_1}(z_1)\cdots u_{\alpha_m}(z_m)$
is an isomorphism $\mathbb A^m\to U$ whose inverse is polynomial. The same
statements hold for every order of $\Phi^+$ compatible with heights.

(ii) $U$ is normalized by $T$, $T\cap U=1$, and
$B=T\cdot U=T\ltimes U$ is a closed connected solvable subgroup with
$\operatorname{Lie}B=\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ and unipotent
radical $U$. It is maximal connected solvable: every connected solvable closed
subgroup of $G$ containing $B$ equals $B$.

(iii) Repeating the construction with the negative roots produces the closed
connected unipotent subgroup $U^-$ with $\operatorname{Lie}U^-=\mathfrak n^-$
and the closed connected solvable subgroup
$B^-=T\cdot U^-=T\ltimes U^-$ with $\operatorname{Lie}B^-=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^-$.

(iv) The restriction of characters is an isomorphism
$X^*(B)\to X^*(T)$, $\chi\mapsto\chi|_T$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be the connected simply connected complex
semisimple affine algebraic group with maximal torus $T$, root system $\Phi$,
simple roots $\Delta$ and positive system $\Phi^+$ of
[[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]], and let
$B=T\ltimes U$ be its Borel subgroup as in
[[lem-semisimple-borel-root-factorization]]. Fix a simple root
$\alpha\in\Delta$, let $U_{-\alpha}$ be the negative root subgroup, let
$\varphi_\alpha:SL_2(\mathbb C)\to G$ and
$n_\alpha=\varphi_\alpha(w)$ be the rank-one homomorphism and Weyl
representative of [[lem-semisimple-rank-one-sl2-root-homomorphism]], and let
$P_\alpha$ be the subgroup generated by $B$ and $U_{-\alpha}$. Then:

(i) $P_\alpha$ is a closed connected algebraic subgroup of $G$ with
$$P_\alpha=B\sqcup Bn_\alpha B,$$
the two double cosets being disjoint;

(ii) $\operatorname{Lie}P_\alpha=\mathfrak b\oplus\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$ and
$\dim P_\alpha=\dim B+1$;

(iii) the coset space $P_\alpha/B$ is $\mathbb P^1$: it is covered by the two
affine charts $z\mapsto u_{-\alpha}(z)B$ and $t\mapsto u_\alpha(t)n_\alpha B$,
each isomorphic to $\mathbb A^1$ and glued by $t=z^{-1}$.

Let $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ be the three-dimensional Lie algebra of
[[def-special-linear-lie-algebra-sl-two]] with its basis $(e,f,h)$, and let
$V$ be a finite-dimensional module over it
([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]).

(i) $V$ is a direct sum of irreducible submodules.
(ii) If $V\ne0$ is irreducible, there is an integer $m\ge0$ with
$\dim V=m+1$ and with $h$ acting diagonalisably with eigenvalues
$m,m-2,\dots,-m$, each on a one-dimensional subspace.
(iii) For arbitrary finite-dimensional $V\ne0$, the operator $h$ acts
diagonalisably on $V$ with integer eigenvalues.

The assignments on $x\in\mathfrak g$

$$\Delta(x)=\iota_{\mathfrak g}(x)\otimes1+1\otimes\iota_{\mathfrak g}(x),\qquad \varepsilon(x)=0,\qquad S(x)=-\iota_{\mathfrak g}(x)$$

extend to the standard cocommutative Hopf-algebra structure on
$U(\mathfrak g)$. The first two assignments are Lie maps into the commutator
algebras of $U(\mathfrak g)\otimes U(\mathfrak g)$ and $k$, so enveloping
universality extends them to algebra maps. Interpreting the last assignment as
a Lie map into $U(\mathfrak g)^{\mathrm{op}}$ extends it to an algebra map into
the opposite algebra, equivalently an anti-algebra map $S$.

Coassociativity, cocommutativity, and the counit identities follow because the
corresponding algebra maps agree on every generator. For the antipode, write
$\Delta(a)=\sum a_{(1)}\otimes a_{(2)}$. Both convolution identities hold on
$1$ and on every generator, since multiplying
$-x\otimes1+1\otimes x$ gives zero. If they hold for $a$ and $b$, then

$$\sum S(a_{(1)}b_{(1)})a_{(2)}b_{(2)}=\sum S(b_{(1)})S(a_{(1)})a_{(2)}b_{(2)}=\varepsilon(a)\varepsilon(b)1,$$

and similarly

$$\sum a_{(1)}b_{(1)}S(a_{(2)}b_{(2)})=\sum a_{(1)}b_{(1)}S(b_{(2)})S(a_{(2)})=\varepsilon(a)\varepsilon(b)1.$$

Induction on word length and linearity therefore prove both antipode
identities on all of $U(\mathfrak g)$.

This remark is non-load-bearing: no later item on this page depends on these
Hopf formulas.

derivations.claim: Write $\kappa=a+ib$ in the real root space. Choose a real number $t$ outside the following finite exceptional set: for each root, exclude a value making $\langle a+tb,\beta^\vee\rangle=0$ unless both pairings already vanish; for each Weyl element, exclude a value making $w(a+tb)=a+tb$ unless $wa=a$ and $wb=b$. Each nonidentical linear equation excludes at most one value. Then the real vector $c=a+tb$ has stabilizer $W_c=W_a\cap W_b=W_\kappa$, and its perpendicular roots are exactly $\Phi_\kappa$. The real closed-chamber stabilizer theorem [F1] therefore identifies $W_\kappa$ with the group generated by these root reflections. The assumed simple system gives $W_\kappa=W_J$. Reduced-word positivity in [F1] gives $m_j=\langle\mu_{j-1},\alpha_j^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$: the inverse prefix sends $\alpha_j$ to a positive root. For completeness, $s_i$ permutes the positive roots other than $\alpha_i$, so $s_i\rho=\rho-\alpha_i$ and $\langle\rho,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=1$. Each positive coroot is a nonzero nonnegative integral sum of simple coroots (apply the positive-root statement to the dual root system), giving the asserted positive integral pairing. The final $\mu_N=w_J\rho$ pairs strictly negatively with every positive coroot of $\Phi_\kappa$.

Choose root generators $e_\alpha,f_\alpha,h_\alpha$ with $[e_\alpha,f_\alpha]=h_\alpha$. In $H_{j-1}$ its highest vector $v$ has $\alpha_j$-weight $m_j-1$, because $\langle\kappa,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle=0$ and $\langle\rho,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle=1$. The identity $e_\alpha f_\alpha^m v=m(a-m+1)f_\alpha^{m-1}v$ for a highest vector of weight $a$, proved by commuting $e_\alpha$ past the $m$ factors, shows that $f_{\alpha_j}^{m_j}v$ is killed by $e_{\alpha_j}$. Every other simple positive generator commutes with $f_{\alpha_j}$ and kills $v$. Thus this is a highest vector of weight $-\kappa-\rho+\mu_j$, defining $H_j\to H_{j-1}$. On the negative-root PBW model it is multiplication on the right by $f_{\alpha_j}^{m_j}$. The associated graded is multiplication by a nonzero monomial in the polynomial algebra $S(\mathfrak n^-)$, hence injective; taking the highest nonzero degree proves injectivity of the original map. Twisting the rational highest weight adds $\kappa+\rho$, so the same map is $B$-equivariant. This gives the fixed chain.

In the highest-weight module $V$ of [F3] put $$V'=\bigoplus_{\mu_N-\xi\notin Q_+}V_\xi,\qquad V''=V/V'.$$ This is a $B$-submodule: raising a weight outside the downset of $\mu_N$ cannot enter that downset, since subtracting a positive root from an element of $Q_+$ stays incompatible with the assumed outside condition in the reverse direction. More explicitly, if $\mu_N-(\xi+\beta)\in Q_+$ for $\beta>0$, then $\mu_N-\xi\in Q_+$, a contradiction. All weights of $V''$ satisfy $\mu_N-\xi\in Q_+$. Its one-dimensional extremal weight line $V_{\mu_N}$ is a $B$-submodule because raising it leaves this downset.

Put $\alpha=\alpha_j$, $m=m_j$ and $C_j=H_{j-1}/H_j$. Let $\mathfrak u^-_\alpha$ be the sum of negative root spaces other than $\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$. It is a Lie subalgebra stable under the $\alpha$-Levi. Ordering its basis before $f_\alpha$ in PBW gives $$C_j\cong U(\mathfrak u^-_\alpha)\otimes \operatorname{span}(v,f_\alpha v,\ldots,f_\alpha^{m-1}v).$$ Indeed $\operatorname{im}H_j$ has exactly the basis with final $f_\alpha$ exponent at least $m$. The last factor is the $m$-dimensional simple $\alpha$-module. Positive root spaces other than $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ kill this factor: commute them past powers of $f_\alpha$; all resulting roots stay positive and different from $\alpha$, or vanish. Therefore this basis identifies $C_j$ with the parabolic induction from that finite-dimensional $\mathfrak p_\alpha$-module. In particular $\pi(e_\alpha)$ and $\pi(f_\alpha)$ are locally nilpotent on $C_j$: the adjoint $\alpha$-action on each finite PBW degree of $U(\mathfrak u^-_\alpha)$ is locally finite, and its tensor with the last factor is a sum of finite-dimensional $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ modules.

Suppose a weight $\xi$ of $V''$ has $\chi_{-\kappa+\xi}=\chi_{-\kappa+\mu_N}$. By [F4] and the $W$-invariance of the sign change, $\kappa-\xi\in W(\kappa-\mu_N)=W(\kappa-\rho)$, where the last equality uses $w_J\kappa=\kappa$. Choose $w$ with $w(\kappa-\xi)=\kappa-\rho$. Then $$\kappa-w\kappa=\rho-w\xi\in Q_+,$$ since $w\xi$ is a weight of $V$ and lies below $\rho$ by [F3]. By [F2] the difference is zero, so $w\kappa=\kappa$ and $w\in W_\kappa=W_J$. Thus $\xi=w^{-1}\rho\in W_J\mu_N$. For a strictly antidominant weight $\mu_N$ in this subsystem, $v\mu_N-\mu_N\in Q_+$ for every $v\in W_J$: telescope a reduced word, whose simple-root pairings with $\mu_N$ are negative and whose prefix roots are positive by [F1]. Consequently $\xi-\mu_N\in Q_+$, whereas $\mu_N-\xi\in Q_+$ by step 2.2. The pointed root cone forces $\xi=\mu_N$. Thus all other weights of $V''$ have central characters different from the distinguished one. This is separation for arbitrary complex antidominant $\kappa$, using no real-chamber restriction.

Remove the integral character $\rho$ from the rational $B$-action on $C_j$. Its infinitesimal action becomes $\pi+\kappa$, and all torus weights are integral, beginning with $\mu_{j-1}-\rho$. This action extends to a rational $P_\alpha$-action. Explicitly keep the torus weight action and the existing positive root groups, and define the additional negative root group by $x_{-\alpha}(t)=\exp(t\pi(f_\alpha))$. This exponential is a finite sum on each vector by step 3.1. On finite PBW-degree subspaces, the Levi $\mathrm{SL}_2$ relations hold by [F6]; the torus action agrees because its $\alpha$-weight is that of $\pi$, as $\kappa(h_\alpha)=0$. The other torus characters are integral and hence rational. The non-Levi positive nilradical acts locally nilpotently and its conjugation relations with the Levi follow by exponentiating the Lie brackets; the finite Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff sums agree with its root-group factorization [F6]. These actions are locally finite: commuting a positive non-Levi root generator through a PBW word never increases its $\mathfrak u^-_\alpha$ degree, and the Levi preserves that degree. Each bounded-degree tensor the last finite factor is finite-dimensional and stable under $\mathfrak p_\alpha$. Hence all the displayed matrix coefficients are regular and glue to the rational parabolic action. Covariance with $\pi(\mathfrak g)$ follows on the root generators by the same bracket/exponential calculation. This is a twisted $(\mathfrak g,P_\alpha)$-module of twist $\kappa$.

Induce $\mathbb C_{-\kappa-\rho}\otimes V''$ from $\mathfrak b$. By exactness of induction, its distinguished weight line induces the submodule $H_N$. The quotient has a finite Verma filtration with one factor $M(-\kappa-\rho+\xi)$ for each other weight, counted with multiplicity: order the finitely many weight spaces from higher to lower and refine within each torus weight space; the positive nilradical raises weights and the torus acts diagonally. Choose a central element $z$ whose value $c_0$ on the distinguished character differs from its values $c_i$ on all the other characters. Such $z$ exists: each forbidden equality is a proper linear hyperplane in the center, and a finite union of proper linear subspaces cannot cover a complex vector space (restrict to the finite span of elements individually separating the finitely many pairs). Let $g(t)=\prod_i(t-c_i)$ with repetition along the quotient filtration. The product $g(z)$ annihilates that quotient, because each factor kills its corresponding successive Verma factor; all factors commute. On $H_N$ it is the nonzero scalar $g(c_0)$. Therefore $g(z)/g(c_0)$ maps the induced module onto $H_N$ and is the identity on $H_N$, giving a projection. It intertwines the rational twisted $B$-action because $z$ is invariant under the adjoint action of connected $B$. This is an actual module projection; no $\mathcal O_X$-linearity is asserted for central operators on arbitrary differential modules.

Apply [F5] to the exact chain in step 2.1. The PBW identity gives $\mathcal E_0=\mathcal D_\kappa\otimes\mathcal O_X(\rho)$. Descent of step 4.1 gives $\mathcal E_{j-1}/\mathcal E_j= \mathcal O_X(\rho)\otimes p_\alpha^\dagger N_j$, with $N_j=\mathsf E^{P_\alpha}_\kappa(C_j)$. These modules are coherent: $\mathcal E_0$ is locally a rank-one free differential module, and the PBW filtered-noetherian argument makes its differential submodules $\mathcal E_j$ and quotients coherent. Locally the quotient has the form $\mathcal O(-1)\boxtimes N_j$; finite differential generators on the two affine fiber charts involve finitely many coefficients in $N_j$. Their base-differential span must be $N_j$, since vertical differentiation creates no new coefficients. The partial TDO is locally noetherian by the same PBW argument, so $N_j$ is coherent.

Composing induction of $V\twoheadrightarrow V''$ with the projection of step 4.2 gives a surjection of twisted modules $$M(-\kappa-\rho)\otimes V\twoheadrightarrow H_N.$$ Here the tensor identity is the map $u\otimes(c\otimes v)\mapsto \sum(u_{(1)}\otimes c)\otimes u_{(2)}v$, with inverse obtained by inserting the antipode in the second enveloping factor. The coproduct and antipode from [F7] check on generators that both maps respect the $\mathfrak b$ relations, are mutual inverses, and commute with the twisted rational $B$-actions. Apply the exact functor [F5]. Its PBW and tensor identities give $\mathcal D_\kappa\otimes_{\mathbb C}V\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal E_N$ with differential action only on $\mathcal D_\kappa$. The sections $1\otimes v_i$ for a finite basis of $V$ are global differential generators. This proves finite global generation and completes all chain assertions, including the empty-word case. Choice enters through the inherited highest-weight and Weyl suppliers and the permitted bases.
